sections.subtitle: „Božji čovjek“: gost koji je i ovaj razgovor najprije predao u molitvu
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić odgovara na pitanje tko je on i opisuje se kao Božji čovjek
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **re:DEFINICIJA** počinje pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip“. Voditelj Krunoslav najavljuje gosta u mjesecu u kojem se obilježava **Dan domovinske zahvalnosti**, odnosno konačno oslobođenje hrvatskog prostora. Gost je **Dario Kordić**. On uzvraća pozdravom „ljubljenoj braći i sestrama u Kristu i hrvatskome rodu“ i izražava nadu da će slušateljima nešto od razgovora ostati zapisano u srcu po Duhu Svetom.

Krunoslav priznaje da ne zna kako bi gosta predstavio jer bi to bilo „jako komplicirano“, pa taj zadatak prepušta njemu. Kordić odgovara jednostavno: **„Na prvu, ja bih rekao da sam Božji čovjek.“** Pojašnjava da nastoji osluškivati Krista i slijediti ga te da sve što čini prije svega predaje Gospodinu u molitvu, pa tako i dolazak na ovo snimanje.

Opisuje i naviku koju je razvio tijekom brojnih svjedočanstava. Nakon svetih misa po Hrvatskoj te Bosni i Hercegovini svjedočio je često zajedno sa suprugom. Prije svakog nastupa zamolio bi petnaestak, dvadeset ili trideset prijatelja, časnih sestara i svećenika da se pomole kako bi nastup bio na slavu Gospodina i kako bi Gospodin dotaknuo ljude. Tako je bilo i ovaj put: za podcast se, kaže, molilo puno ljudi. Krunoslav zaključuje da se to već osjeća i da će razgovor donijeti mnogo plodova.
sections.subtitle_en: “Man of God”: the guest who first surrendered even this conversation into prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić answers the question of who he is and describes himself as a man of God
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the podcast **re:DEFINICIJA** begins with the greeting “Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph”. The host Krunoslav announces the guest in the month in which **Homeland Thanksgiving Day** is observed, that is, the final liberation of Croatian territory. The guest is **Dario Kordić**. He responds with a greeting to the “beloved brothers and sisters in Christ and the Croatian people” and expresses hope that something from the conversation will remain written in the listeners' hearts through the Holy Spirit.

Krunoslav admits that he does not know how he would introduce the guest because that would be “very complicated”, so he leaves that task to him. Kordić answers simply: **“At first, I would say that I am a man of God.”** He explains that he strives to listen to Christ and follow him, and that everything he does he first of all surrenders to the Lord in prayer, including coming to this recording.

He also describes a habit he developed during numerous testimonies. After Holy Masses throughout Croatia and Bosnia and Hercegovina, he often gave testimony together with his wife. Before each appearance, he would ask about fifteen, twenty, or thirty friends, nuns, and priests to pray so that the appearance would be to the glory of the Lord and so that the Lord would touch people. It was so this time as well: many people, he says, prayed for the podcast. Krunoslav concludes that this is already felt and that the conversation will bring much fruit.

sections.subtitle: Djetinjstvo na rijeci Bosni: krave, konji i ministriranje kod svetog Ante
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić se s osmijehom prisjeća djetinjstva u Žepču
sections.content:
Na Krunoslavljevo pitanje o odrastanju Kordić odgovara s očitom nostalgijom. Djetinjstvo je proveo u **Žepču**, „malom gradiću na rijeci Bosni“, koji naziva divnim krajem. Ondje je završio prva četiri razreda osnovne škole, išao u crkvu **svetog Ante Padovanskog**, ministrirao i kupao se u rijeci Bosni.

O roditeljima kaže da mu je majka bila liječnica koja je radni vijek započela upravo u Žepču, a otac veterinar. Obitelj je živjela na rubu grada, pokraj farmi krava. Kordić se sjeća koliko je s ocem obilazio krave i konje koje je otac liječio. Pamti i intervencije kad bi se krava „udavila“ jabukom koju je trebalo izvaditi.

Iz tog vremena posebno pamti veliki orah i kokoši u dvorištu. Djetinjstvo opisuje kao „predivno za doživjeti“ i ističe da ga se uvijek prisjeća s radošću: **„prelijepo je bilo“**.
sections.subtitle_en: Childhood on the river Bosna: cows, horses, and altar serving at Saint Anthony
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić recalls his childhood in Žepče with a smile
sections.content_en:
To Krunoslav's question about growing up, Kordić responds with evident nostalgia. He spent his childhood in **Žepče**, „a small town on the river Bosna“, which he calls a wonderful region. There he completed the first four grades of elementary school, went to the church of **Saint Anthony of Padua**, served as an altar boy, and swam in the river Bosna.

Regarding his parents, he says that his mother was a physician who began her working life precisely in Žepče, and his father was a veterinarian. The family lived on the edge of town, next to cow farms. Kordić remembers how much he visited cows and horses with his father that his father treated. He also remembers interventions when a cow would „choke“ on an apple that had to be removed.

From that time, he particularly remembers the large walnut tree and the chickens in the yard. He describes his childhood as „wonderful to experience“ and emphasizes that he always recalls it with joy: **„it was beautiful“**.

sections.subtitle: Busovača, novinarstvo i snježna večer kad je upoznao Veneru
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o prvom susretu sa suprugom Venerom u automobilu nakon plesa
sections.content:
Voditelj najavljuje da je Domovinski rat sigurno bio prijelomni trenutak u gostovu životu, ali najprije ga pita o upoznavanju supruge **Venere**. Kordić objašnjava da se obitelj 1971. preselila u **Busovaču**, gradić u središnjoj Bosni udaljen šezdesetak ili sedamdesetak kilometara od Žepča, prema Sarajevu. Ondje je završio drugu polovicu osnovne škole. Gimnaziju je pohađao u **Vitezu**, gdje će poslije ići i njegova supruga, a novinarstvo je studirao u **Sarajevu**.

Primjećuje da su on i Venera živjeli stotinjak metara jedno od drugoga, a ipak su se upoznali slučajno. Bila je snježna večer. On i jedan prijatelj išli su po prijateljevu rođakinju na ples, a s njom se s plesa vraćala i Venera. Sjeli su u isti automobil i tako su se upoznali. Veza nije počela odmah, no „iskrica se zapalila“, pa su pet ili šest mjeseci kasnije, tog ljeta, počeli hodati.

O supruzi govori s dubokim poštovanjem. **„Gospodin je uveo Veneru u moj život. Ona je najveći dar“**, kaže. Ističe da je upravo ona nosila najveći dio patnje koju je on poslije proživljavao: odgajala je djecu i nosila obitelj. Naziva je sveticom i kaže da nije dostojan izgovoriti ni slovo o njoj. Sve što vrijedi, zaključuje, došlo mu je u život preko nje i preko Gospodina.
sections.subtitle_en: Busovača, journalism, and the snowy evening when he met Venera
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts his first meeting with his wife Venera in a car after a dance
sections.content_en:
The host announces that the Homeland War was certainly a turning point in the guest's life, but first asks him about meeting his wife **Venera**. Kordić explains that the family moved in 1971 to **Busovača**, a small town in central Bosnia about sixty or seventy kilometers from Žepče, towards Sarajevo. There he finished the second half of elementary school. He attended high school in **Vitez**, where his wife would also go later, and he studied journalism in **Sarajevo**.

He notes that he and Venera lived about a hundred meters from each other, yet they met by chance. It was a snowy evening. He and a friend went to pick up the friend's cousin from a dance, and Venera was also returning from the dance with her. They sat in the same car and that is how they met. The relationship did not begin immediately, but "a spark was ignited," so five or six months later, that summer, they started dating.

He speaks of his wife with deep respect. **"The Lord brought Venera into my life. She is the greatest gift,"** he says. He emphasizes that it was precisely she who carried the greatest part of the suffering that he later experienced: she raised the children and carried the family. He calls her a saint and says that he is not worthy to speak even a letter about her. Everything of worth, he concludes, came into his life through her and through the Lord.

sections.subtitle: Od tvorničkog novinara do predstojnika ureda obrane
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić opisuje rad u uredu obrane u Busovači uoči rata
sections.content:
Vjenčali su se **1986. godine**. Krunoslav u šali dodaje da je to godina njegova rođenja, a Kordić napominje da je od tada prošlo četrdeset godina. Ubrzo je stigao sin **Vladimir**. U to vrijeme Kordić je radio kao novinar u jednoj tvornici. Tada nastupaju demokratske promjene i on se, mlad i, kako kaže, nošen srcem poput mnogih Hrvata, uključuje u politička zbivanja. Naglašava da je i to vodio Gospodin: „Nije ništa bilo moje.“

Nakon prvih demokratskih izbora HDZ je u Busovači bio među pobjedničkim strankama, a Kordić je preuzeo dužnost **predstojnika ureda obrane**. Posao mu se tada uglavnom svodio na savjetovanje mladića da ne odlaze u takozvanu JNA. Pritom ističe da to nisu bili samo Hrvati, nego i muslimani i drugi.

Rata u Hrvatskoj još nije bilo, ali se, kako kaže, „osjećalo sve što slijedi“. Kad je Hrvatska počela gorjeti, iz središnje Bosne okupljali su mladiće i slali ih u pomoć **Dubrovniku i Slavoniji**. Neki od njih poginuli su već u prvim danima. To je bio Kordićev prvi doticaj s ratom.
sections.subtitle_en: From factory journalist to head of the defense office
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić describes work in the defense office in Busovača on the eve of the war
sections.content_en:
They were married in **the year 1986**. Krunoslav jokingly adds that this is the year of his birth, and Kordić notes that forty years have passed since then. Soon their son **Vladimir** arrived. At that time, Kordić worked as a journalist in a factory. Then democratic changes occurred, and he, young and, as he says, carried by the heart like many Croats, got involved in political events. He emphasizes that the Lord guided this as well: „Nothing was mine.“

After the first democratic elections, HDZ was among the winning parties in Busovača, and Kordić assumed the duty of **head of the defense office**. His work at that time mainly came down to advising young men not to go to the so-called JNA. At the same time, he emphasizes that these were not only Croats, but also Muslims and others.

There was no war in Croatia yet, but, as he says, „everything that was to follow was felt“. When Croatia began to burn, they gathered young men from central Bosnia and sent them to help **Dubrovnik and Slavonija**. Some of them were killed already in the first days. That was Kordić's first contact with war.

sections.subtitle: Dopredsjednik Herceg-Bosne osnovane na dan pada Vukovara
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o osnivanju Hrvatske zajednice Herceg-Bosne 18. studenoga 1991.
sections.content:
Kordić kaže da ga je vrijeme „izguralo“ da vrlo mlad bude izabran za **dopredsjednika Hrvatske zajednice Herceg-Bosne**. Zajednica je osnovana **18. studenoga 1991.**, upravo na dan pada Vukovara. Sebe opisuje kao „samo jednakog“ među ostalima.

Pojašnjava da Hrvati Bosne i Hercegovine tada ni u kojem slučaju nisu željeli ostati u „krnjoj Jugoslaviji“. Donijeli su odluku da u takav sastav ne žele ući, a pritom su, kako kaže, uvijek osluškivali što je najbolje.

Dok je Hrvatska gorjela, pripremali su se i oni, a plamen je ubrzo zahvatio cijelu Bosnu i Hercegovinu. Kordić tvrdi da su Hrvati tada objektivno bili najspremniji dočekati prvi udar velikosrpske agresije. Nabraja mjesta stradanja, od sela **Ravno**, koje je prvo gorjelo 1991., do Kupresa, Posavine, Hercegovine i središnje Bosne 1992. Ističe da su Hrvati tada branili i one koji nisu bili spremni, misleći na muslimane, te da su podnijeli prvi udar: „Ne tražimo mi neku zahvalnost, ali to su činjenice i treba ih poštivati.“
sections.subtitle_en: Vice President of Herceg-Bosna founded on the day of the fall of Vukovar
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the founding of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna on November 18, 1991.
sections.content_en:
Kordić says that time "pushed him out" to be elected as a very young man as **vice president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna**. The community was founded on **November 18, 1991**, precisely on the day of the fall of Vukovar. He describes himself as "just an equal" among the others.

He clarifies that the Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time by no means wanted to remain in a "rump Yugoslavia". They made the decision that they did not want to enter such an arrangement, and at the same time, as he says, they always listened closely to what was best.

While Croatia was burning, they were preparing as well, and the flames soon engulfed all of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Kordić claims that Croats at that time were objectively the most prepared to meet the first strike of Greater Serbian aggression. He lists places of suffering, from the village of **Ravno**, which was the first to burn in 1991, to Kupres, Posavina, Hercegovina, and central Bosnia in 1992. He emphasizes that Croats at that time also defended those who were not prepared, referring to Muslims, and that they bore the first strike: "We are not asking for some gratitude, but those are the facts and they should be respected."

sections.subtitle: „Narodni tribun“ među rovovima i agregatima
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić objašnjava da se u ratu doživljavao kao narodni tribun i glas branitelja
sections.content:
Krunoslav naglašava da je Kordić u ratu imao političku, a ne vojnu odgovornost. Gost potvrđuje da nikada nije bio u vojsci. Prisjeća se da su ga tijekom suđenja odvjetnici pitali kako bi opisao svoju ulogu, a on je odgovorio da je bio **„nekakav narodni tribun“**.

Sebe je doživljavao kao glas hrvatskih branitelja u središnjoj Bosni i cijeloj Herceg-Bosni. Obrane hrvatskog prostora bile su zadaća HVO-a i vojske, a on je bio svojevrsni glasnogovornik potreba hrvatskoga naroda i onaj koji je davao vjeru. Njegove zadaće uključivale su:

- obilazak rovova i razgovore sa svakim braniteljem HVO-a,
- redovite tiskovne konferencije,
- posjete obiteljima branitelja i sudjelovanje na sprovodima,
- pomoć svakome u potrebi, „neovisno samo Hrvatu“.

Tiskovne konferencije održavale su se i u najkritičnijim trenucima, dok je oko njih gorjelo, u improviziranim uvjetima, bez struje i uz agregate. Kordić kaže da tada nije bio svjestan koliko je ljudima ta „živa riječ“ značila. Tada nije razmišljao ni o tome da je posrijedi Božja volja i Božja misija. Tek mu je u zatočeništvu, kaže, Gospodin dao „pregled svega“ i pokazao da je sve činio On, a ne on sam, iako je možda mislio da je on najviše učinio.
sections.subtitle_en: "People's Tribune" Among Trenches and Generators
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić explains that during the war he perceived himself as a people's tribune and the voice of the defenders
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav emphasizes that Kordić had political, not military responsibility during the war. The guest confirms that he was never in the army. He recalls that during the trial the lawyers asked him how he would describe his role, and he answered that he was **"a kind of people's tribune"**.

He perceived himself as the voice of Croatian defenders in central Bosnia and throughout Herceg-Bosna. Defending the Croatian territory was the task of the HVO and the army, while he was a kind of spokesman for the needs of the Croatian people and the one who gave faith. His tasks included:

- visiting the trenches and talking with every HVO defender,
- regular press conferences,
- visits to the families of defenders and attending funerals,
- helping anyone in need, "not only a Croat."

Press conferences were held even in the most critical moments, while everything burned around them, under improvised conditions, without electricity and with generators. Kordić says that back then he was not aware of how much that "living word" meant to the people. At that time, he did not even think about the fact that it was God's will and God's mission. Only while in captivity, he says, did the Lord give him "an overview of everything" and showed him that He did everything, and not he himself, even though he might have thought that he had done the most.

sections.subtitle: Lašvanska dolina: dvanaest mjeseci u okruženju u kojem „ni ptica nije mogla doći“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira američkog časnika Charlesa Shradera o okruženju Hrvata u Lašvanskoj dolini
sections.content:
Kordić slušateljima koji slabije poznaju prilike opisuje zborno područje HVO-a u središnjoj Bosni. Ono je obuhvaćalo Žepče, Usoru, Kakanj, Vareš, Zenicu, Lepeničku dolinu s Kiseljakom, Kreševom i Fojnicom, zatim **Lašvansku dolinu**, Vrbasku dolinu s Jajcem i Bugojnom te Uskoplje do Kupresa.

O uzroku sukoba između muslimana i Hrvata, koji naziva nepotrebnim i krvavim, kaže da je svakome žao svake žrtve. Ipak, tvrdi da treba biti realan. Prema njegovim riječima, Srbi su očistili najveći dio prostora i „vrlo smišljeno“ usmjerili prognanike prema središnjoj Bosni. Hrvatski prognanici većinom su odlazili prema Hrvatskoj ili na zapad, a muslimanski su ostajali u Travniku, Bugojnu i drugim mjestima gdje je stanovništvo dotad bilo „pola-pola“. Umjesto da ih se potakne na povratak prostora izgubljenih od Srba, netko im je, kaže, poručio: „Ovo je sad vaš Eldorado… samo ga trebate osvojiti od mekšeg protivnika.“ Tako je, po njegovu tumačenju, krenula agresija na Hrvate.

Poziva se na **Charlesa Shradera**, visokog američkog časnika koji je svjedočio na njegovu suđenju i napisao knjigu o ratu u središnjoj Bosni. Shrader je, prema Kordiću, rekao: „Nemojte gluposti govoriti da Hrvati iz Lašvanske doline mogu nekoga napasti koji su u totalnom okruženju.“ Okruženje je trajalo gotovo dvanaest mjeseci i obuhvaćalo Busovaču, Vitez, Novi Travnik i Novu Bilu. U Novoj Biloj je djelovala franjevačka bolnica u kojoj su se ranjenici liječili u crkvenim klupama.

Žrtve su bile goleme. Vitez je imao oko 12.000 stanovnika po popisu i nisu svi ostali u ratu, a ondje je, prema Kordiću, poginulo oko **700 ljudi**. U Busovači je poginulo oko 250. Spominje i travničko groblje Prahulje puno hrvatskih branitelja, brigadu Ban Jelačić iz Kiseljaka te Žepče, Jajce, Bugojno i Uskoplje: „Svatko je imao svoju priču.“
sections.subtitle_en: Lašva Valley: twelve months in an encirclement in which "not even a bird could come"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes American officer Charles Shrader on the encirclement of Croats in the Lašva Valley
sections.content_en:
Kordić describes the HVO operational zone in central Bosnia to listeners who are less familiar with the circumstances. It encompassed Žepče, Usora, Kakanj, Vareš, Zenica, the Lepenica Valley with Kiseljak, Kreševo, and Fojnica, then the **Lašva Valley**, the Vrbas Valley with Jajce and Bugojno, and Uskoplje up to Kupres.

Regarding the cause of the conflict between Muslims and Croats, which he calls unnecessary and bloody, he says that everyone regrets every victim. Still, he claims that one needs to be realistic. According to his words, the Serbs cleansed most of the area and "very deliberately" directed the displaced persons toward central Bosnia. Croatian displaced persons mostly went toward Croatia or to the west, while the Muslim ones stayed in Travnik, Bugojno, and other places where the population until then had been "half-and-half". Instead of encouraging them to regain the areas lost to the Serbs, someone, he says, told them: "This is your Eldorado now… you just need to conquer it from a softer opponent." That is how, according to his interpretation, the aggression against the Croats began.

He refers to **Charles Shrader**, a high-ranking American officer who testified at his trial and wrote a book about the war in central Bosnia. Shrader, according to Kordić, said: "Do not talk nonsense that the Croats from the Lašva Valley who are in a total encirclement can attack anyone." The encirclement lasted almost twelve months and encompassed Busovača, Vitez, Novi Travnik, and Nova Bila. A Franciscan hospital operated in Nova Bila, in which the wounded were treated in church pews.

The casualties were enormous. Vitez had about 12,000 residents according to the census and not all stayed in the war, and there, according to Kordić, about **700 people** were killed. In Busovača, about 250 were killed. He also mentions the Travnik cemetery Prahulje full of Croatian defenders, the Ban Jelačić Brigade from Kiseljak, as well as Žepče, Jajce, Bugojno, and Uskoplje: "Everyone had their own story."

sections.subtitle: Krunica oko vrata svakog branitelja
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić govori o krunici kao izvoru snage pod granatama
sections.content:
Usred priče o ratnim stradanjima Kordić ističe ono što smatra presudnim. Vojnici i političari mogli su činiti sve što su mogli, ali su majke, očevi, bake, djedovi, supruge i djeca pod granatama, skrivajući se u skloništima, **molili krunicu**.

„Ta krunica je davala snagu i bila je oko vrata svakog hrvatskog branitelja“, kaže. Kao jednako važne ističe i svećenike koji su ostali s narodom. Sve to naziva sudbonosnim.

Zaključuje da je Gospodin htio da Hrvati ostanu „na ostacima ostataka“. Nisu se održali na svakom dijelu prostora, ali Kordić zahvaljuje Bogu što su opstali u središnjoj Bosni, **„u nadi protiv svake nade“**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Rosary around the neck of every defender
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić speaks about the Rosary as a source of strength under shells
sections.content_en:
In the midst of the story of war suffering, Kordić highlights what he considers crucial. Soldiers and politicians could do everything they could, but mothers, fathers, grandmothers, grandfathers, wives, and children under shells, hiding in shelters, **prayed the Rosary**.

„That Rosary gave strength and was around the neck of every Croatian defender“, he says. As equally important, he also highlights the priests who stayed with the people. He calls all of that fateful.

He concludes that the Lord wanted Croats to remain „on the remnants of remnants“. They did not hold out in every part of the area, but Kordić thanks God that they survived in central Bosnia, **„in hope against all hope“**.

sections.subtitle: Obitelj koja nije otišla i pogled na Ahmiće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost započinje odgovor na pitanje što se dogodilo u Ahmićima
sections.content:
Krunoslav napominje da je Venera tijekom rata ostala u Bosni iako je imala priliku otići u Hrvatsku. Zatim postavlja ključno pitanje: **što se zapravo dogodilo u Ahmićima**, zbog kojih je Kordić završio u Haagu?

Kordić najprije potvrđuje da su u ratu ostali supruga, troje djece (Vladimir, Marija i najmlađa Elizabeta), njezini i njegovi roditelji te braća i sestre. Objašnjava da se to podrazumijevalo: ako od drugih traži da izdrže, mora i sam dati primjer, s obitelji koja dijeli „i dobro i zlo“.

O Ahmićima govori kao političar koji je, kaže, pratio i znao što se događa. Izražava tugu zbog žrtava i želi pokoj vječni svim poginulima, „i na našoj i na njihovoj strani“. Ipak, smatra da se ne smiju iznositi neistine, pa navodi svoje argumente:

- selo je, tvrdi, bilo **vojni cilj** s naoružanim ljudima, a u njemu su poginuli i hrvatski branitelji, što po njegovu mišljenju ne bi bilo moguće da je riječ o nebranjenom cilju;
- i suci koje opisuje kao njemu nesklone utvrdili su, prema njegovim riječima, da su neki ciljevi bili legitimni, primjerice ako se s minareta pucalo iz trocijevca;
- prostor je bio strateški: da je tog jutra presječena cesta, Lašvanska bi dolina bila podijeljena i Hrvati u njoj, smatra, ne bi opstali.

Posebno ga žalosti, kaže, uveličavanje brojki. Na njegovu suđenju spominjalo se **76 poginulih**, a njegove i druge procjene govore o šezdesetak. Ne želi ulaziti u to, ali naglašava da je tragedija jednaka i sa 60 i sa 76 poginulih te da s godinama ne treba „ići na 116“. Uspoređuje to s rastom brojki kakav se događao kod Jasenovca. Ističe da time ne želi umanjiti žrtvu nego tražiti poštivanje činjenica i svake žrtve: „Istina će nas sve osloboditi.“
sections.subtitle_en: The family that did not leave and a perspective on Ahmići
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest begins the answer to the question of what happened in Ahmići
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that Venera remained in Bosnia during the war even though she had the opportunity to leave for Croatia. Then he asks the key question: **what actually happened in Ahmići**, because of which Kordić ended up in The Hague?

Kordić first confirms that during the war his wife, three children (Vladimir, Marija, and the youngest Elizabeta), her and his parents, as well as brothers and sisters remained. He explains that this was taken for granted: if he asks others to endure, he must also lead by example, with a family that shares "both good and evil".

About Ahmići he speaks as a politician who, he says, followed and knew what was happening. He expresses grief over the victims and wishes eternal rest to all the fallen, "both on our side and on their side". Nevertheless, he believes that untruths must not be presented, so he states his arguments:

- the village was, he claims, a **military target** with armed men, and Croatian defenders also died in it, which in his opinion would not have been possible if it were an undefended target;
- even the judges whom he describes as unfavorable to him established, according to his words, that some targets were legitimate, for example if there was shooting from a minaret with a triple-barrel gun;
- the area was strategic: had the road been cut that morning, the Lašvanska dolina would have been divided and the Croats in it, he believes, would not have survived.

He is particularly saddened, he says, by the exaggeration of numbers. At his trial, **76 fallen** was mentioned, and his and other estimates speak of about sixty. He does not want to get into that, but emphasizes that the tragedy is the same with both 60 and 76 fallen and that over the years one should not "go to 116". He compares this to the inflation of numbers that happened with Jasenovac. He emphasizes that he does not wish to diminish the sacrifice with this, but to ask for respect for facts and for every victim: "The truth will set us all free."

sections.subtitle: Pljuvanje na mrežama, argumenti iz presude i jedna domovina u srcu
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić spominje Luku Mišetića i njegove objave na Twitteru o presudi
sections.content:
Kordić kaže da nema Facebook ni druge društvene mreže i da ih ne prati. Ponekad mu supruga pokaže što se piše. Na takve napade, koji idu „od pečenja djeteta do ovoga, onoga“, nikada nije odgovarao.

Kao osobu „najviše verziranu za Ahmiće“ navodi **Luku Mišetića**, odvjetnika **Ante Gotovine**. Prema Kordiću, Mišetić je na Twitteru, na dan najžešćih napada, pozvao odvjetnike iz Sarajeva da s njim rasprave konkretne članke i aline presude u predmetu Kordić: „Nemojte govoriti ono što nema u presudi.“ Nitko se, kaže Kordić, nikada nije imenom i prezimenom odazvao da argumentima, a ne histerijom, suoči stavove.

Navodi i nedavni primjer koji ga je pogodio. Poslali su mu snimku na kojoj šef pravne katedre u **Zenici** pred djecom petog i šestog razreda uspoređuje Hrvatsku, hrvatski narod i hrvatske zastave s **Trećim Reichom**. „Ne ide to tako govoriti, a želimo graditi budućnost zajedničke domovine“, upozorava. Poziva na traženje zajedničkog rješenja kako bi država funkcionirala.

Na kraju iznosi svoje osobno stajalište: domovina je za njega jedna, a to je Hrvatska. Kroz povijest je bila „ovaka i onaka“, danas je u dvije države, ali on u srcu ne dijeli Hrvatsku i Bosnu i Hercegovinu: **„ona je jedna za mene“**.
sections.subtitle_en: Spitting on social networks, arguments from the verdict, and one homeland in the heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić mentions Luka Mišetić and his posts on Twitter about the verdict
sections.content_en:
Kordić says that he does not have Facebook or other social networks and that he does not follow them. Sometimes his wife shows him what is being written. To such attacks, which go „from roasting a child to this, that“, he has never responded.

As the person „most well-versed in Ahmići“ he cites **Luka Mišetić**, the attorney of **Ante Gotovina**. According to Kordić, Mišetić on Twitter, on the day of the fiercest attacks, called on lawyers from Sarajevo to discuss with him the specific articles and paragraphs of the verdict in the Kordić case: „Do not say what is not in the verdict.“ No one, says Kordić, has ever responded by first and last name to confront views with arguments, and not hysteria.

He also cites a recent example that affected him. They sent him a recording in which the head of the law department in **Zenica**, in front of fifth- and sixth-grade children, compares Croatia, the Croatian people, and Croatian flags to the **Third Reich**. „It won't do to speak like that, while we want to build the future of a common homeland“, he warns. He calls for seeking a common solution so that the state might function.

In the end, he presents his personal stance: for him the homeland is one, and that is Croatia. Throughout history it was „like this and like that“, today it is in two states, but in his heart he does not divide Croatia and Bosnia and Hercegovina: **„it is one for me“**.

sections.subtitle: Optužnica, život u ilegali i poruka Tuđmanu i Šušku: „Zovite me, ja ću tog dana ići“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da se nikada nije želio skrivati te da je bio spreman dragovoljno otići u Haag
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita kako je doživio poziv u Haag: je li otišao dragovoljno ili je osjećao averziju i razočaranje. Kordić odgovara da nije bilo ni averzije ni bilo kakvog negativnog raspoloženja.

Optužnica je stigla oko **Daytonskog sporazuma**, rješenja koje Kordić naziva nepravednim: zaustavilo je rat, ali nije donijelo rješenje. S optužnicom je živio godinu i pol. Dio tog vremena kretao se slobodno, a dio proveo u nekoj vrsti ilegale, ne znajući ni od koga se skriva ni gdje.

Ipak, naglašava da se nikada nije želio skrivati. Vrhovništvu Hrvatske, predsjedniku **Tuđmanu** i ministru **Šušku**, poručio je: „Kada bude najbolje za Hrvatsku, ja sam tu. Zovite me, ja ću tog dana ići.“ Tako je i bilo. Kad je osjetio da je došao trenutak, otišao je jer se, kaže, nije imao zbog čega skrivati i htio je čuti što imaju protiv njega i njegove „braće“. Tada je u Haag otišlo desetak Hrvata.
sections.subtitle_en: Indictment, life underground, and a message to Tuđman and Šušak: „Call me, I will go that day“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that he never wanted to hide and that he was ready to go to The Hague voluntarily
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks how he experienced the summons to The Hague: whether he went voluntarily or felt aversion and disappointment. Kordić replies that there was neither aversion nor any negative sentiment.

The indictment arrived around the time of the **Dayton Agreement**, a solution that Kordić calls unjust: it stopped the war, but it did not bring a solution. He lived with the indictment for a year and a half. Part of that time he moved about freely, and part he spent in a kind of underground existence, knowing neither whom he was hiding from nor where.

Nevertheless, he emphasizes that he never wanted to hide. To the supreme leadership of Croatia, President **Tuđman** and Minister **Šušak**, he sent word: „When it is best for Croatia, I am here. Call me, I will go that day.“ And so it was. When he felt that the moment had arrived, he went because, he says, he had nothing to hide for and he wanted to hear what they had against him and his „brothers“. At that time, about ten Croats went to The Hague.

sections.subtitle: 6. listopada 1997.: na ribičkom stolcu NATO-ova aviona, s krunicom u ruci
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić se prisjeća leta iz Splita za Nizozemsku
sections.content:
Kordić se jasno sjeća datuma: **6. listopada 1997.**, sunčan dan u splitskoj zračnoj luci. Ondje je dao kratku izjavu koju je na engleski prevodio prevoditelj iz Ureda predsjednika Tuđmana. Prisutan je bio i američki visoki predstavnik **Gelbard**.

Nakon ispraćaja ukrcali su se u stari NATO-ov zrakoplov bez pravih sjedala, umjesto kojih su bili ribički stolci. Kordić je sjeo, s krunicom u ruci, i tijekom leta do Nizozemske utonuo u san.

Prvi dan u Haagu uzeli su mu otiske prstiju i fotografirali ga, a zatim je ušao u sobu u kojoj će ostati ne znajući koliko dugo. Od prvog dana uzeo je krunicu. Kaže da Gospodinu nikada nije postavio pitanje koliko će to trajati. Molio je samo: **„Gospodine, nemoj mi otvoriti vrata dok ne bude tvoja volja.“** Dodaje da bi prihvatio i Božju volju da nikada ne izađe.
sections.subtitle_en: October 6, 1997: on a fishing chair of a NATO plane, with a Rosary in hand
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić recalls the flight from Split to the Netherlands
sections.content_en:
Kordić clearly remembers the date: **October 6, 1997**, a sunny day at the Split airport. There he gave a brief statement translated into English by an interpreter from the Office of President Tuđman. The American high representative **Gelbard** was also present.

After the send-off, they boarded an old NATO airplane without real seats, in place of which were fishing chairs. Kordić sat down, with a Rosary in hand, and during the flight to the Netherlands fell into sleep.

The first day in The Hague they took his fingerprints and photographed him, and then he entered the room in which he would stay not knowing for how long. From the first day he took up the Rosary. He says that he never asked the Lord the question of how long it would last. He only prayed: **„Lord, do not open the door for me until it is your will.”** He adds that he would also have accepted God's will never to come out.

sections.subtitle: Osamnaest mjeseci duhovne obnove u ćeliji dva sa četiri metra
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje ćeliju sa željeznim krevetom i improviziranim oltarićem
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita je li optužnicu doživio kao izdaju svega što je učinio za hrvatski narod u Bosni. Kordić se najprije obraća voditelju imenom i napominje da su na „ti“ jer se poznaju iz javne molitve krunice na trgovima. Zatim objašnjava da je bio tužan, ali ne samo zbog sebe, nego i zbog mnogih iz vojnog i političkog vodstva Hrvata u Lašvanskoj dolini koji su optuženi, „znajući što je stvarno bilo“. Prema njegovim riječima, Hrvati su bili napadnuti, a neutralni promatrači procijenili su odnos snaga na **7 do 10 prema 1** u korist onih koji su ih držali u okruženju.

Ipak, kaže, Bog čovjeka stvori „borcem“. Uzeo je krunicu i molio. Do prvog izlaska u sudnicu prošlo je **18 mjeseci** u pripremama, uz povremene posjete odvjetnika. Kordić ih je iskoristio, kako kaže, „u najboljem smislu“: kao životnu duhovnu obnovu kakvu nikada nije prošao „ni prije ni poslije“ i koju je osobno vodio Gospodin. „Dao mi je ruku i po toj sobici sam ja s njime tisuće puta prošao“, opisuje. Gospodin ga je, kaže, čistio od grijeha, egoizma i „svih natruha“.

Ćelija je bila dva sa četiri metra, sa željeznim krevetom, stolićem i improviziranim oltarićem sa svetim slikama. Iz nje je izlazio samo u šetnju i u dnevni boravak. To razdoblje uspoređuje s majkom koja nedonošče hrani majčinim mlijekom: Gospodin mu je tada davao „nektar“ za sve što će uslijediti.
sections.subtitle_en: Eighteen months of spiritual renewal in a two by four meter cell
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the cell with an iron bed and an improvised little altar
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks whether he experienced the indictment as a betrayal of everything he did for the Croatian people in Bosnia. Kordić first addresses the host by name and notes that they are on informal "you" terms because they know each other from the public praying of the Rosary on squares. Then he explains that he was sad, but not only because of himself, but also because of many from the military and political leadership of the Croats in the Lašva Valley who were indicted, "knowing what truly happened." According to his words, the Croats were attacked, and neutral observers estimated the balance of power at **7 to 10 to 1** in favor of those holding them surrounded.

Nevertheless, he says, God creates man as a "fighter." He took the Rosary and prayed. Until his first appearance in the courtroom, **18 months** passed in preparations, with occasional visits from lawyers. Kordić used them, as he says, "in the best sense": as a life spiritual renewal such as he had never undergone "either before or after" and which the Lord personally led. "He gave me His hand and through that little room I walked with Him thousands of times," he describes. The Lord, he says, cleansed him of sin, egoism, and "all traces of impurities."

The cell was two by four meters, with an iron bed, a small table, and an improvised little altar with holy images. He only left it for a walk and into the common room. He compares that period to a mother who feeds a premature baby with mother's milk: the Lord was giving him the "nectar" then for everything that was to follow.

sections.subtitle: Tri sata ujutro, uoči prvog ročišta: „Tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi“
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić opisuje svjetlo koje ga je probudilo u tri sata ujutro i prvi susret sa živim Bogom
sections.content:
Nakon 18 mjeseci došao je **12. travnja 1999.**, dan kad je s optuženikom iz istog predmeta, „subratom“ Marijom Čerkezom, prvi put trebao izaći u sudnicu. Večer prije legao je, kako kaže, s „radosnim nestrpljenjem“, pomolio se i zaspao.

„U tri sata budi me svjetlo koje nije od ovoga svijeta. To je moj prvi susret sa živim Bogom“, svjedoči. Na Krunoslavljevo pitanje je li to bio san, odgovara da je bio budan i da je jednostavno znao da je Gospodin ondje. Svjetlo je obasjalo mračnu prostoriju, a doživljaj uspoređuje s onim što je doživjela sveta **Faustina Kowalska** sa zrakama.

Kaže da je od radosti „useptao“, ne znajući što reći, a u srcu je čuo glas: **„Dragi moj sine, dragi moj prijatelju, ne boj se, s tobom sam uvijek i u svemu, tvoju parnicu ću ja voditi.“**

Od tog dana, objašnjava, u ljudskom je smislu činio sve što je mogao. Opisuje raspored u sudnici: odvjetnici malo dalje od njega, svjedok još dalje, suci uzdignuti s lijeve strane, a tužitelj na drugoj strani. Pitanja koja bi se sjetio pisao je na papiriće koje je stražar nosio obrani. Ipak, znao je da će biti onako kako je Božja volja. Tog jutra nazvao je suprugu i rekao joj da se osjeća kao leptirić koji lebdi: „Oni neka rade što žele, a meni je kao da na svadbu idem.“ Ta „svadba“, dodaje, traje do danas.
sections.subtitle_en: Three o'clock in the morning, on the eve of the first hearing: "I will lead your trial"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić describes the light that woke him at three in the morning and his first encounter with the living God
sections.content_en:
After 18 months came **April 12, 1999**, the day when, together with the defendant from the same case, his "confrere" Marijo Čerkez, he was to enter the courtroom for the first time. The night before, he went to bed, as he says, with "joyful impatience", prayed, and fell asleep.

"At three o'clock, a light that is not of this world wakes me. That is my first encounter with the living God," he testifies. To Krunoslav's question about whether that was a dream, he answers that he was awake and that he simply knew that the Lord was there. The light illuminated the dark room, and he compares the experience to what Saint **Faustina Kowalska** experienced with the rays.

He says that out of joy he "was breathless", not knowing what to say, and in his heart he heard a voice: **"My dear son, my dear friend, do not be afraid, I am with you always and in everything, I will lead your trial."**

From that day, he explains, in human terms he did everything he could. He describes the layout in the courtroom: the lawyers a little further from him, the witness even further, the judges elevated on the left side, and the prosecutor on the other side. The questions he would think of he wrote on small pieces of paper that the guard carried to the defense. Still, he knew that it would be as God's will is. That morning he called his wife and told her that he felt like a little butterfly hovering: "Let them do whatever they want, but to me it feels like I am going to a wedding." That "wedding", he adds, lasts to this day.

sections.subtitle: Papa Ivan Pavao II. „visok kao Biokovo“ i klica duhovnog poziva
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje viđenje pape Ivana Pavla II. iznad Veprica
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da je to bilo mistično iskustvo, uz ogradu da ne zna je li izraz teološki točan. Kordić potvrđuje da je takvih susreta bilo još dva ili tri, ali o većini ne želi govoriti.

Izdvaja posljednji, iz **2003. godine**, uoči proglašenja blaženim **Ivana Merza** u Banjoj Luci. Probudio se i ugledao svetog oca **papu Ivana Pavla II.**, „visokog kao Biokovo“, iznad **Veprica**. Taj kraj dobro poznaje jer je ondje često ljetovao još kao dijete. Papa mu je pružio ruku i dva-tri puta ga pozvao, a Kordić se pred njim osjećao „kao mali miš“. Uzvratio mu je ruku.

U tom iskustvu danas vidi klicu duhovnog poziva koji tada nije prepoznao. Postupno ga je razaznavao tek deset-petnaest godina kasnije, u razgovorima sa svećenicima. Od tada je, kaže, njegov hod za Kristom postao intenzivniji.
sections.subtitle_en: Pope John Paul II „as tall as Biokovo“ and the seed of a spiritual vocation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes a vision of Pope John Paul II above Vepric
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that it was a mystical experience, with the caveat that he does not know whether the expression is theologically accurate. Kordić confirms that there were two or three more such encounters, but he does not want to speak about most of them.

He singles out the last one, from **2003**, on the eve of the beatification of **Ivan Merz** in Banja Luka. He woke up and saw the Holy Father **Pope John Paul II**, „as tall as Biokovo“, above **Vepric**. He knows that region well because he often spent summer holidays there even as a child. The Pope extended his hand to him and called him two or three times, and Kordić felt before him „like a little mouse“. He extended his hand back to him.

In that experience today, he sees the seed of a spiritual vocation that he did not recognize at the time. He gradually discerned it only ten to fifteen years later, in conversations with priests. Since then, he says, his walk after Christ has become more intense.

sections.subtitle: Scheveningen: bodljikava žica, „podmornica“ i dvadeset mjeseci suđenja
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić opisuje pritvorsku jedinicu u Scheveningenu i zgradu zvanu podmornica
sections.content:
Pritvorska jedinica nalazila se u **Scheveningenu**, malom primorskom mjestu koje Kordić opisuje kao mondeno turističko odredište. Galebovi su doletjeli dok su bili u šetnji, „ali mi smo bodljikavom žicom bili ograđeni“.

Prve četiri godine proveo je u zgradi koju su zatvorenici zvali **„podmornica“**. Ondje se nije mogao otvoriti nijedan prozor, a zrak se ubacivao umjetno kroz instalacije koje se nisu čistile. Bio je to, kaže, „život pod staklenim zvonom“. Zgrada je imala 32 sobe. Kad je optuženika bilo sve više, premješteni su u objekt nazvan **„96“** prema broju soba, gdje se prozor barem mogao malo odškrinuti. U svakoj sobi bio je po jedan zatvorenik.

Suđenje je trajalo **20 mjeseci**, svakoga dana od ponedjeljka do petka, „od jutra do mraka“. U Haag su ga vozili u lisicama i uz posebne mjere, a pri dolasku i povratku slijedili su pregledi i skidanje. Kordić zaključuje kratko: „Procedure su se obavljale, proces je trajao.“
sections.subtitle_en: Scheveningen: barbed wire, „submarine“ and twenty months of trial
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić describes the detention unit in Scheveningen and the building called the submarine
sections.content_en:
The detention unit was located in **Scheveningen**, a small seaside town that Kordić describes as a fashionable tourist destination. Seagulls flew in while they were on a walk, „but we were fenced in with barbed wire“.

He spent the first four years in the building that the prisoners called the **„submarine“**. Not a single window could be opened there, and air was pumped in artificially through installations that were not cleaned. It was, he says, „life under a bell jar“. The building had 32 rooms. When there were more and more accused, they were moved to a facility named **„96“** after the number of rooms, where the window could at least be cracked open a little. In each room there was one prisoner.

The trial lasted **20 months**, every day from Monday to Friday, „from morning to dark“. They drove him to The Hague in handcuffs and under special measures, and upon arrival and return, searches and undressing followed. Kordić concludes briefly: „Procedures were carried out, the process went on.“

sections.subtitle: Gospine poruke iz „plave knjige“ i presuda od 25 godina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost se prisjeća izricanja prvostupanjske presude u veljači 2001.
sections.content:
Kordić se usput prisjeća da je tih dana, uz Bibliju, čitao Gospine poruke oca **Gobbija**, takozvanu **„plavu knjigu“**. U najtežim danima uvijek bi naišao na neku lijepu Gospinu poruku koja bi ga „osokolila“. Ističe da je bio pun Duha Svetoga i radostan unatoč svemu te da tuge nije bilo ni u trenucima presude.

Prvostupanjska presuda izrečena je krajem **veljače 2001.**: **25 godina zatvora**. Supruga i odvjetnici bili su optimistični, a Kordić je za tu prigodu obukao hrvatsko odijelo, narodnu nošnju koju je dobio iz Trogira. Ipak, kaže, u srcu je osjećao da ishod neće biti onakav kakvom su se nadali.

Presudnim smatra iznenađenje iz posljednjih sedam dana postupka. Pojavio se svjedok kojeg su, prema Kordiću, pripremali 30 dana i koji je bio smješten na katu iznad njega, a da obrana to nije znala. Svjedok je trebao potvrditi da je Kordić one noći bio na sastanku na kojem se razgovaralo o Ahmićima. Kordić naglašava da to za njega ne bi bio zločin ni da je bio ondje, ali tvrdi da sedam dana prije ni sedam dana poslije uopće nije išao u taj grad. Svjedok je, kaže, rekao samo da je „čuo“ da je on bio ondje.

Obrana je dovela sve ljude koje je svjedok naveo kao navodne sudionike sastanka. Nizozemski vještaci pregledali su bilježnicu u koju je vojna policija upisivala tko dolazi kod zapovjednika zbornog područja. Kordićeva imena u njoj nije bilo. Vještaci su potvrdili da je bilježnica originalna, da listovi nisu iskidani te su vještačili čak i olovku. Ipak, sud te argumente nije prihvatio.

Kao ilustraciju koliko je optužba, po njegovu mišljenju, stajala „na labavim nogama“, Kordić navodi tužiteljevu rečenicu „Vjerujte nam na riječ“ i slikovitu usporedbu. Kao da mačku ulove kako pije mlijeko ponedjeljkom i srijedom, pa tvrde da je to sigurno činila i ostalim danima, iako to ne mogu dokazati. Presuda je, zaključuje, donesena „na temelju indicija i priča“.
sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's messages from the "blue book" and the 25-year sentence
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls the pronouncement of the first-instance verdict in February 2001
sections.content_en:
Kordić recalls in passing that in those days, alongside the Bible, he read Our Lady's messages of Father **Gobbi**, the so-called **"blue book"**. In the hardest days, he would always come across some beautiful message from Our Lady that would "encourage" him. He emphasizes that he was full of the Holy Spirit and joyful despite everything, and that there was no sorrow even in the moments of the verdict.

The first-instance verdict was pronounced at the end of **February 2001**: **25 years of imprisonment**. His wife and lawyers were optimistic, and for that occasion Kordić put on a Croatian suit, a national costume he had received from Trogir. Nevertheless, he says, in his heart he felt that the outcome would not be what they had hoped for.

He considers decisive the surprise from the last seven days of the proceedings. A witness appeared who, according to Kordić, had been prepared for 30 days and who had been accommodated on the floor above him, without the defense knowing it. The witness was supposed to confirm that Kordić was at the meeting that night where Ahmići was discussed. Kordić emphasizes that for him that would not have been a crime even if he had been there, but he claims that seven days before and seven days after he did not go to that town at all. The witness, he says, only stated that he had "heard" that he was there.

The defense brought all the people whom the witness named as alleged participants in the meeting. Dutch experts examined the notebook in which the military police recorded who came to the commander of the operative zone. Kordić's name was not in it. The experts confirmed that the notebook was authentic, that pages had not been torn out, and they even forensically examined the pen. Nevertheless, the court did not accept those arguments.

As an illustration of how much the indictment, in his opinion, stood "on shaky legs", Kordić cites the prosecutor's sentence "Take our word for it" and a vivid comparison. As if a cat is caught drinking milk on Mondays and Wednesdays, and then they claim that it certainly did so on the other days as well, even though they cannot prove it. The verdict was, he concludes, delivered "on the basis of circumstantial evidence and stories".

sections.subtitle: Promjena vlasti u Hrvatskoj i američki odvjetnici koji su branili bez plaće
sections.screenshot_description: Kordić govori o uskraćivanju financiranja obrane nakon promjene vlasti
sections.content:
Uslijedio je **žalbeni postupak**, u kojem je obrana mogla iznijeti dodatne dokaze. Kordić se pritom našao u, kako kaže, specifičnim okolnostima. U Hrvatskoj je došlo do promjene vlasti, a na predsjednika Tuđmana i ministra Šuška „žestoko se obrušavalo“. Njegovoj obrani uskraćena su prava dogovorena još za njihova mandata, pa nova vlast odvjetnike više nije željela plaćati.

Kordić je tada odvjetnicima rekao da ga više ne moraju braniti jer im to nitko neće platiti. No odvjetnici iz Amerike ostali su s njim i vodili postupak još tri godine, u nadi da će neka buduća vlast podmiriti troškove. Obeštećeni nisu bili nikada, a neki od njih danas više nisu živi. „Kad ljudi stranci vam urade tri-četiri godine besplatno obranu…“, kaže s vidljivom zahvalnošću.

To razdoblje opisuje kao posebnu ostavljenost i križ koji je, kako kaže, doživio od „svojih“, uz napomenu da riječ stavlja „pod navodne znakove“. Tvrdi i da su tada falsificirani neki dokumenti te da su u tome sudjelovali i pojedini ministri tadašnje hrvatske vlade. Imena ne želi spominjati, ali dodaje da je to bilo poznato javnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Change of government in Croatia and American lawyers who defended without pay
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kordić speaks about the denial of defense funding after the change of government
sections.content_en:
The **appeals process** followed, in which the defense could present additional evidence. Kordić found himself in, as he says, specific circumstances. A change of government took place in Croatia, and President Tuđman and Minister Šušak "were fiercely attacked." His defense was denied the rights agreed upon during their mandate, so the new government no longer wanted to pay the lawyers.

Kordić then told the lawyers that they no longer had to defend him because no one would pay them for it. But the lawyers from America stayed with him and led the proceedings for another three years, in the hope that some future government would cover the costs. They were never compensated, and some of them are no longer alive today. "When people, foreigners, do a defense for you for three or four years for free...", he says with visible gratitude.

He describes that period as a special abandonment and a cross that, as he says, he experienced from "his own," noting that he puts the word "in quotation marks." He also claims that certain documents were falsified at that time and that individual ministers of the Croatian government at the time participated in it. He does not want to mention names, but adds that this was known to the public.

sections.subtitle: „Gospe, nemoj da mi mrvice sa stola daju“: žalbena presuda bez umanjenja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje svoj vapaj međugorskoj Gospi pred čitanje žalbene presude
sections.content:
Ulazeći u sudnicu na izricanje konačne presude, Kordić je, kako kaže, jedini put zavapio **međugorskoj Majci**: „Gospe, usliši me, ali nek bude opet Božja volja. Nemoj da mi mrvice sa stola daju.“ Osjećao je da je obrana podnijela toliko dokaza da mu kazna mora biti smanjena. Upravo zato nije htio da u javnosti ispadne kako mu je netko „velikodušno nešto dao“.

Opisuje i ozračje suđenja. U prvom stupnju sudac i tužitelj bili su Englezi, kao i svjedoci iz UNPROFOR-a, a obranu su činili američki odvjetnici i hrvatski dio tima. Petočlanim žalbenim vijećem predsjedao je Nijemac.

Predsjednik vijeća pročitao je da mu se **skida sedam od 21 točke**, među njima Busovača i Novi Travnik, ali ne i Ahmići. Po logici stvari, kaže Kordić, kazna je trebala biti smanjena za trećinu, kao što je to, tvrdi, bivalo svakome dok je postojao Haaški sud. Sudac je ipak izrekao: **„Unatoč tome vaša kazna ostaje 25 godina.“**

Kordić se, kako kaže, u sebi „blago raspio“, a supruga je pustila suzu. Ona je znala za što je on molio Gospu. Kao majka i supruga koja se borila s djecom, sve je doživljavala teže.

Zatim je počelo čekanje na to koliko će još ostati u Haagu. Ostale Hrvate koji nisu bili na njegovu katu viđao je samo na misama. Tako je, godinu dana prije svog odlaska iz Haaga, na nekoliko misa vidio i **generala Gotovinu**. S Hrvatima s istog kata družio se u šetnji i dnevnom boravku.
sections.subtitle_en: "Our Lady, do not let them give me crumbs from the table": appeals judgment without reduction
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes his cry to Our Lady of Međugorje before the reading of the appeals judgment
sections.content_en:
Entering the courtroom for the delivery of the final judgment, Kordić, as he says, cried out for the only time to the **Mother of Međugorje**: "Our Lady, hear me, but let God's will be done again. Do not let them give me crumbs from the table." He felt that the defense had submitted so much evidence that his sentence had to be reduced. Precisely because of that, he did not want it to appear in public that someone had "generously given him something."

He also describes the atmosphere of the trial. In the first instance, the judge and prosecutor were English, as were the witnesses from UNPROFOR, and the defense consisted of American lawyers and the Croatian part of the team. The five-member appeals chamber was presided over by a German.

The presiding judge of the chamber read that **seven of the 21 counts were being dropped**, among them Busovača and Novi Travnik, but not Ahmići. By the logic of things, Kordić says, the sentence should have been reduced by a third, as, he claims, happened to everyone while the Hague Tribunal existed. The judge nevertheless pronounced: **"Notwithstanding that, your sentence remains 25 years."**

Kordić, as he says, "mildly broke down" inside, and his wife shed a tear. She knew what he had prayed to Our Lady for. As a mother and wife who struggled with the children, she experienced everything more heavily.

Then began the wait for how much longer he would stay in The Hague. He saw the other Croats who were not on his floor only at Masses. Thus, a year before his departure from The Hague, he also saw **General Gotovina** at several Masses. With the Croats from the same floor, he associated during walks and in the common room.

sections.subtitle: Iz Haaga u Graz: zatvor u „Ulici Božje Poljane“ i oklada koju su zatvorenici izgubili
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje dolazak u zatvor Karlau i veliku sobu s osam zatvorenika
sections.content:
Nakon gotovo **punih devet godina** u pritvoru u Haagu, Dario Kordić upućen je na izdržavanje kazne u jednu od europskih država koje su s Međunarodnim sudom za bivšu Jugoslaviju potpisale sporazum o izvršenju kazni. Upravnik ga je pitao ima li želju kamo bi otišao. Mogao je spomenuti sestru u Njemačkoj, no Kordić je, kako kaže, odgovor prepustio Bogu: „Gospodine, gdje ti misliš da je najbolje, pošalji me.“

Poslan je u zatvor najbliži Hrvatskoj, **Karlau u Grazu**. Sam ističe da se zatvor nalazi u ulici Herrgottwiesgasse, što prevodi kao **Ulica Božje Poljane**. Nakon samice u kojoj je, kako kaže, bio „sa Gospodinom“, smješten je u najveću sobu u tom zatvoru, sa sedmero zatvorenika s raznih kontinenata. Među njima je bio i jedan Hrvat koji ga je dočekao.

Cimeri su već prvoga dana, bez njegova znanja, otvorili **kladionicu**. Okladili su se da će novi zatvorenik izdržati najviše 30 dana, a onda zatražiti premještaj ondje gdje nema dima, droge i tučnjava. Mjesec je prošao, a Kordić je u toj sobi ostao još osam godina. Kroz nju je, prema njegovu računu, prošlo **91 zatvorenika**. Ističe da nikada nije doživio ni ružan pogled, a kamoli nešto gore.

### Krunica i sveta voda među pripadnicima drugih vjera

Među cimerima bilo je malo katolika, a mnogo Arapa i muslimana. Kordić je svakoga od njih ujutro blagoslivljao svetom vodom, javno i pred svima, i nitko mu nikada nije prigovorio. Nakon petnaestak dana zatvorenici su sami počeli dolaziti s molbama: „Dario, hoćeš se pomoliti za ovo ili ono?“ Dok su oni za stolom kockali, „kao u filmovima“, on je šetao s krunicom i molio za svakoga od njih. Naglašava da je toj molitvi pristupao odgovorno i da nikoga tko ga je zamolio nikada nije odbio.
sections.subtitle_en: From The Hague to Graz: Prison on "God's Field Street" and the Bet the Prisoners Lost
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes his arrival at Karlau prison and the large room with eight prisoners
sections.content_en:
After almost **a full nine years** in detention in The Hague, Dario Kordić was sent to serve his sentence in one of the European states that had signed an agreement on the enforcement of sentences with the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. The warden asked him if he had a wish where he would go. He could have mentioned his sister in Germany, but Kordić, as he says, left the answer to God: "Lord, wherever you think is best, send me."

He was sent to the prison closest to Croatia, **Karlau in Graz**. He points out himself that the prison is located on Herrgottwiesgasse street, which he translates as **God's Field Street**. After solitary confinement in which he was, as he says, "with the Lord," he was placed in the largest room in that prison, with seven prisoners from various continents. Among them was also a Croat who welcomed him.

On the very first day, without his knowledge, his roommates opened a **betting pool**. They bet that the new prisoner would last at most 30 days, and then ask for a transfer to where there is no smoke, drugs, and fights. A month passed, and Kordić stayed in that room for another eight years. According to his count, **91 prisoners** passed through it. He emphasizes that he never experienced even a bad look, let alone something worse.

### The Rosary and Holy Water Among Members of Other Faiths

Among his roommates there were few Catholics, and many Arabs and Muslims. Kordić blessed each of them in the morning with holy water, publicly and in front of everyone, and no one ever objected to him. After about fifteen days, the prisoners themselves began to come with requests: "Dario, will you pray for this or that?" While they gambled at the table, "like in the movies," he walked with the Rosary and prayed for each of them. He emphasizes that he approached that prayer responsibly and that he never refused anyone who asked him.
