sections.subtitle: Dvije i pol godine molitve: kako je slika vraga ustupila mjesto Lurdskoj Gospi
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić pripovijeda kako je cimer poderao sliku vraga i zatražio sliku Gospe
sections.content:
Voditelj Krunoslav podsjeća gosta na jedno svjedočanstvo iz Graza koje je Kordić, kako sam kaže, često pričao: priču o dvije slike, Gospinoj i Sotoninoj.

Kordić najprije opisuje posljednjih pet godina zatočeništva, provedenih uglavnom s ljudima s prostora bivše države. Hrvata gotovo nije bilo, nego su to većinom bili **Srbi, muslimani i Albanci**. Upravo s njima, ističe, provodio je Božiće koji su mu ostali posebni. Pripremali bi mu ih, a on bi odlazio na ponoćku koja se služila danju, u crkvi na njegovu katu. Kasnije bi u sobi upalio svijeće, a cimeri bi ustali i molili zajedno s njim, „s punim poštovanjem“. Tog se vremena, kaže, sjeća s radošću, iako je, „kao i u svakoj sobi“, bilo svega i svačega.

Iznad svog željeznog kreveta imao je:
- **križ**,
- **sliku Presvetoga Trojstva**,
- **fotografiju svoje obitelji**,
- **sliku Lurdske Gospe** koju su mu s hodočašća poslali hrvatski branitelji, slika koja se mijenja ovisno o kutu gledanja.

Tada je u sobu došao zatvorenik koji je na ormar, osamdesetak do sto centimetara od Kordićeva uzglavlja, zalijepio veliku i iznimno ružnu sliku vraga. Sobe su bile pod reflektorima pa je pogled na nju bio neizbježan, i noću pri odlasku u toalet i ujutro pri buđenju.

Kordić tom zatvoreniku nikada ništa nije rekao jer je, kako objašnjava, to bio njegov prostor i njegov ormar. Umjesto toga **ustrajno je molio** da mu Bog dotakne srce. Nakon otprilike **dvije i pol godine** cimer ga je jednog poslijepodneva pozvao pred svima i rekao: „Dario, vrijeme je da ovaj đavo ide s ovoga.“ Sliku je poderao jednom, zatim još jednom, bacio je u koš te upitao bi li mu Kordić dao sliku Gospe da je zalijepi na isto mjesto. Gospina slika ondje je ostala do kraja Kordićeva zatočeništva.

„Pa samo da sam to doživio, a doživio sam stotine još drugih stvari“, zaključuje Kordić, uvjeren da je Božja ruka vodila svaki trenutak njegova boravka u zatvoru.
sections.subtitle_en: Two and a half years of prayer: how a picture of the devil gave way to Our Lady of Lourdes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić recounts how his roommate tore up a picture of the devil and asked for a picture of Our Lady
sections.content_en:
The host Krunoslav reminds the guest of a testimony from Graz that Kordić, as he himself says, often told: the story of two pictures, Our Lady's and Satan's.

Kordić first describes the last five years of captivity, spent mostly with people from the territory of the former state. There were almost no Croats, but they were mostly **Serbs, Muslims, and Albanians**. It was precisely with them, he emphasizes, that he spent Christmases that remained special to him. They would prepare them for him, and he would go to Midnight Mass which was celebrated during the day, in the church on his floor. Later he would light candles in the room, and the roommates would stand up and pray together with him, „with full respect“. He remembers that time, he says, with joy, although, „as in every room“, there was a bit of everything.

Above his iron bed he had:
- **a cross**,
- **a picture of the Holy Trinity**,
- **a photograph of his family**,
- **a picture of Our Lady of Lourdes** that Croatian veterans sent him from a pilgrimage, a picture that changes depending on the viewing angle.

Then a prisoner came into the room who pasted a large and exceptionally ugly picture of the devil onto a wardrobe, about eighty to one hundred centimeters from Kordić's headboard. The rooms were under floodlights, so looking at it was unavoidable, both at night when going to the toilet and in the morning upon waking up.

Kordić never said anything to that prisoner because, as he explains, that was his space and his wardrobe. Instead, **he perseveringly prayed** for God to touch his heart. After about **two and a half years**, one afternoon his roommate called him in front of everyone and said: „Dario, it is time for this devil to go from this.“ He tore the picture once, then once more, threw it into the trash can, and asked if Kordić would give him a picture of Our Lady to paste in the same place. Our Lady's picture remained there until the end of Kordić's captivity.

„Even if I had experienced only that, and I experienced hundreds of other things as well“, Kordić concludes, convinced that God's hand guided every moment of his stay in prison.

sections.subtitle: Venera i troje djece: život od Božje providnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o tome kako je supruga Venera preživljavala oslanjajući se na Božju providnost
sections.content:
Krunoslav potom pita kako je bez muža živjela **Venera** s troje male djece. Napominje da je u početku uživala određena prava, a da su kasnije i ta prava i novac izostali.

Kordić objašnjava da je obitelj, dok je bio živ predsjednik **Tuđman**, imala sve potrebno, i od Hrvatske i od Bosne i Hercegovine. Potpora Hrvata iz BiH trajala je do upada tenkova u **Hercegovačku banku**, oko 2002. godine. Kordić ističe da te događaje zna samo iz medija jer tada nije bio na slobodi. Nakon toga su prestale i te mogućnosti.

Od tog trenutka, kaže Kordić, supruga počinje živjeti „od **Božje providnosti**“. Mnogo puta mu je svjedočila kako bi otišla pred Presveto ili u malu kapelicu svetog Ante na Svetom Duhu i zavapila Gospodinu. Ne bi prošlo ni 24 sata, a njezine bi materijalne potrebe bile riješene, i to preko ljudi od kojih to nitko ne bi očekivao. Kordić iz toga izvlači i osobnu pouku: ne treba se uzdati u ljude za koje misliš da ti nešto duguju, jer pomoć često dolazi od nekoga koga uopće ne poznaješ.

### Odojak i bor s Trešnjevačkog placa

Kao ilustraciju supružine vjere Kordić navodi jednu anegdotu. Bilo je vrijeme Božića, a u kući su sjedili kumovi pred kojima je Venera često ponavljala „Božja providnost“. Kum se našalio: „Pa hajde sad, sad će tebi netko doći, pokucati na vrata i donijeti odojak i bor.“

Ubrzo je zazvonilo. Na vratima je stajao čovjek s **Trešnjevačkog placa**: „Ja sam ovdje poslan, je li ovdje živi supruga Darija Kordića? Moj gazda je poslao bor, poslao odojak, poslao ovo, ono.“ Kordić naglašava da je to bilo svjedočanstvo upravo za kumove koji su sjedili za stolom, jer supruzi, kako kaže, takav dokaz nije ni trebao.
sections.subtitle_en: Venera and Three Children: Living on God's Providence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about how his wife Venera survived by relying on God's providence
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav then asks how **Venera** lived without a husband with three young children. He notes that in the beginning she enjoyed certain rights, and that later both those rights and money ceased.

Kordić explains that the family, while President **Tuđman** was alive, had everything needed, both from Croatia and from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The support of Croats from BiH lasted until the raid of tanks into **Hercegovačka banka**, around the year 2002. Kordić emphasizes that he knows these events only from the media because at that time he was not free. After that, those possibilities also ceased.

From that moment, Kordić says, his wife begins living “on **God's providence**”. Many times she witnessed to him how she would go before the Blessed Sacrament or into the small chapel of Saint Anthony on Sveti Duh and cry out to the Lord. Not even 24 hours would pass, and her material needs would be resolved, and that through people from whom no one would expect it. Kordić also draws a personal lesson from this: one should not rely on people who you think owe you something, because help often comes from someone you do not know at all.

### Suckling Pig and Christmas Tree from Trešnjevački plac

As an illustration of his wife's faith, Kordić recounts an anecdote. It was Christmas time, and the godparents were sitting in the house, in front of whom Venera often repeated “God's providence”. The godfather joked: “Well, come on now, now someone will come to you, knock on the door, and bring a suckling pig and a Christmas tree.”

Soon the doorbell rang. At the door stood a man from **Trešnjevački plac**: “I was sent here, does the wife of Dario Kordić live here? My boss sent a Christmas tree, sent a suckling pig, sent this, that.” Kordić emphasizes that this was a testimony precisely for the godparents who were sitting at the table, because his wife, as he says, did not even need such proof.

sections.subtitle: „Ja želim doći“: posao u Alfi i majka koja je bila i otac
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje suprugin prvi radni dan, kad je pješice kroz snijeg došla na posao
sections.content:
Zahvaljujući dobrim ljudima, Venera je dobila posao u **Alfi**. Kordić ističe da je vlasnik tvrtke pokazao veliko srce. Ponudio joj je plaću bez obveze dolaska na posao: „Hajde dođi, Venera, pa ti budi ovdje, davat ćemo ti plaću. Ne moraš ni raditi.“ Ona je ponudu odbila riječima: „Ja nisam na to naučila, ja želim doći.“

Prvi radni dan u Zagrebu je napadalo **70 centimetara snijega**. Venera je od Trešnjevke do radnog mjesta na Novoj vesi došla pješice i bila je jedina zaposlenica koja se toga dana pojavila. Kordić dodaje da i danas radi u školstvu, u istoj izdavačkoj kući, i da se bori „s osmijehom na licu“. Opisuje je kao **najveseliju ženu na svijetu**, kojoj nitko nikada nije mogao vidjeti na licu koliko je patila.

### Odgoj bez oca

Patnja je ipak bila stvarna. Venera je, kaže Kordić, morala biti i otac i majka, i sinu i kćerima. Posebno je teško bilo sa sinom u adolescenciji, koji je poput mnogih mladića prolazio kroz sve izazove toga doba, a uz to je s **Bad Blue Boysima** putovao po Europi. U detalje Kordić ne želi ulaziti i kaže samo da je „sve to iza nas“.

Molitvom je, ističe, Gospodin sve okrenuo nabolje. Kad se vratio iz zatvora, troje djece već je bilo na putu da postanu obiteljski ljudi, a danas to i jesu. Najmlađa kći imala je tek nešto više od godine dana kada je otišao u Haag. On je stigao na njezin **maturalni ples 2014. godine**, nedugo nakon izlaska iz zatvora.
sections.subtitle_en: "I want to come": a job at Alfa and a mother who was also a father
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes his wife's first working day, when she came to work on foot through the snow
sections.content_en:
Thanks to good people, Venera got a job at **Alfa**. Kordić emphasizes that the owner of the company showed a big heart. He offered her a salary without the obligation of coming to work: "Come on, come, Venera, and you just be here, we will give you a salary. You don't even have to work." She rejected the offer with the words: "I am not used to that, I want to come."

On the first working day, **70 centimeters of snow** fell in Zagreb. Venera came on foot from Trešnjevka to her workplace at Nova ves and was the only employee who showed up that day. Kordić adds that she still works in education today, in the same publishing house, and that she fights "with a smile on her face." He describes her as **the most cheerful woman in the world**, on whose face no one could ever see how much she suffered.

### Upbringing without a father

The suffering was nevertheless real. Venera, Kordić says, had to be both a father and a mother, to both the son and the daughters. It was especially difficult with their son during adolescence, who, like many young men, went through all the challenges of that age, and in addition traveled around Europe with the **Bad Blue Boys**. Kordić does not want to go into details and says only that "all of that is behind us."

Through prayer, he emphasizes, the Lord turned everything for the better. When he returned from prison, the three children were already on the way to becoming family people, and today they are. The youngest daughter was only a little over a year old when he went to The Hague. He made it to her **prom in 2014**, shortly after his release from prison.

sections.subtitle: „Slobodniji u rešetkama nego svi ljudi na svijetu“
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić objašnjava zašto se u zatvoru osjećao slobodnije nego danas
sections.content:
Govoreći o dvanaest godina provedenih na slobodi, Kordić iznosi tvrdnju koja na prvi pogled zvuči paradoksalno: „Ja uvijek kažem, ja sam slobodniji bio u rešetkama od svih ljudi na svijetu. Ja sam bio najslobodniji tada. Ova mi je sloboda manje slobodna nego ona iz zatvora.“

Supruga ga, priznaje, zna zadirkivati da „s čežnjom gleda na ono zatvoreničko vrijeme“. Kordić to slikovito objašnjava: u zatvoru bi ujutro u miru skuhao čaj i uzeo meda, dok u današnjem dnevnom ritmu „nema ni čajeva, ni medova, samo te lomi“.

### Povratak na petak, dan križa

Krunoslav pita je li se vratio **6. lipnja**. Kordić potvrđuje i ističe da mu je posebno drago što je to bio **petak**, dan Isusove muke i križa. Tu iznosi i jedno od svojih životnih načela:

> „Ja ljubim taj križ Isusov i kad nešto previše dobro ide na ovom životu, ja se zabrinem. Dok pljuju, dok napadaju, dok nešto je teško, ja kažem: Hvala ti, Bože, na tvom smo putu.“
sections.subtitle_en: “Freer behind bars than all the people in the world”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić explains why he felt freer in prison than today
sections.content_en:
Speaking about twelve years spent in freedom, Kordić makes a claim that sounds paradoxical at first glance: “I always say, I was freer behind bars than all the people in the world. I was the freest then. This freedom of mine is less free than the one from prison.”

His wife, he admits, sometimes teases him that he “looks with longing at that prison time.” Kordić vividly explains this: in prison in the morning he would make tea in peace and take honey, while in today's daily rhythm “there are neither teas nor honeys, it just breaks you.”

### Return on Friday, the day of the cross

Krunoslav asks if he returned on **June 6**. Kordić confirms and emphasizes that he is especially glad that it was a **Friday**, the day of Jesus' passion and the cross. Here he also presents one of his life principles:

> “I love that cross of Jesus, and when something goes too well in this life, I get worried. While they spit, while they attack, while something is difficult, I say: Thank You, God, we are on Your path.”

sections.subtitle: Bez zahtjeva za pomilovanje: izlet u Mariazell i sveti Bernard na slici
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje sliku svetog Bernarda čija se glava spaja s glavom raspetog Krista
sections.content:
Krunoslav zatim pita gosta za odlazak u **Mariazell** dok je bio u Grazu. Kordić prije odgovora otkriva odluku koju je, kako kaže, donio samostalno, „dok je bio pri pameti“: **nikada neće podnijeti zahtjev za pomilovanje**. „Kad bude Božja volja, izaći ću.“

Prema njegovim riječima, Bog je nadahnuo ljude iz **austrijskog pravosuđa**. Oni su u dva navrata pisali da „ovaj čovjek više kod nas u Austriji ne treba biti“, a Kordić te dopise i danas čuva. Iz Haaga je stigao odgovor da je „rano“. Godine 2014., kad je iza sebe imao gotovo 17 godina zatočeništva, posjetila ga je jedna Španjolka iz **Crvenog križa** s viješću da ni tog ljeta nema šanse i da će se o njegovu slučaju odlučivati tek nakon Božića, 2015. godine. Kordić kaže da je to već bio prihvatio.

### Neplanirano zaustavljanje

Tada mu je zatvorski dušobrižnik (*Seelsorger*) javio da je zajedno s još četvoricom zatvorenika određen za **socijalni izlazak**, na svetu misu u Mariazellu, uz stražu i u lisicama. Vožnja je trajala, prisjeća se, sat i pol do dva.

Usput su stali u gradić za koji Kordić misli da se zvao **Neuberg**. Ondje se nalazi crkva sagrađena po uzoru na staru crkvu iz Njemačke, nekadašnja katedrala i **cistercitski samostan**, danas uglavnom napušten. Među stotinama slika Kordićevu je pažnju privukla jedna: **sveti Bernard** kleči na klecalu pred raspetim Kristom, a njihove su glave umjetnički spojene u jednu.

U tom trenutku, pred kraj zatočeništva, Kordić je u srcu osjetio Gospodinove riječi: to je ono što je izrekao **sveti Pavao**, „ne živim više ja, živi Krist u meni“. Kaže da mu je ta misao često dolazila, a sada mu je Gospodin pokazao njezino značenje.

### „Ideš doma“

U Mariazellu je jedan od slavitelja mise bio **fra Šimun Oreč**, župnik u jednoj austrijskoj župi, koji ga je često posjećivao u zatvoru i kod kojega je Kordić ponekad izlazio. Tijekom mise, kao i onda kad je kod presude zamolio Gospu, u srcu je začuo glas: **„Ideš, ideš doma. Ideš doma.“** Odmah se zapitao kako će ići doma kad su mu upravo rekli da neće.
sections.subtitle_en: No request for pardon: a trip to Mariazell and Saint Bernard in the painting
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes the painting of Saint Bernard whose head merges with the head of the crucified Christ
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav then asks the guest about going to **Mariazell** while he was in Graz. Before answering, Kordić reveals a decision that, as he says, he made independently, “while he was in his right mind”: **he will never submit a request for pardon**. “When it is God's will, I will get out.”

According to his words, God inspired people from the **Austrian judiciary**. On two occasions they wrote that “this man should no longer be with us in Austria,” and Kordić still keeps those letters today. A response arrived from The Hague that it was “early.” In 2014, when he had almost 17 years of captivity behind him, a Spanish woman from the **Red Cross** visited him with the news that there was no chance that summer either and that his case would be decided only after Christmas, in 2015. Kordić says he had already accepted that.

### Unplanned stop

Then the prison chaplain (*Seelsorger*) informed him that, together with four other prisoners, he was designated for a **social outing**, to Holy Mass in Mariazell, with guards and in handcuffs. The drive lasted, he recalls, an hour and a half to two hours.

Along the way they stopped in a small town that Kordić thinks was called **Neuberg**. Located there is a church built after the model of an old church from Germany, a former cathedral and a **Cistercian monastery**, today largely abandoned. Among hundreds of paintings, one caught Kordić's attention: **Saint Bernard** is kneeling on a kneeler before the crucified Christ, and their heads are artistically joined into one.

At that moment, near the end of captivity, Kordić felt the Lord's words in his heart: that is what **Saint Paul** uttered, “it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me”. He says that this thought often came to him, and now the Lord showed him its meaning.

### “You are going home”

In Mariazell, one of the celebrants of the Mass was **fra Šimun Oreč**, a parish priest in an Austrian parish, who often visited him in prison and with whom Kordić sometimes went out. During the Mass, just like when at the verdict he asked Our Lady, he heard a voice in his heart: **“You are going, you are going home. You are going home.”** He immediately wondered how he would go home when they had just told him he would not.

sections.subtitle: Posljednja noć u zatvoru, zaustavljeni zrakoplov i Drava ispod krila
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić pripovijeda o posljednjoj noći u zatvoru s Afganistancem i Alžircem
sections.content:
Već sljedećeg dana u njegovu je sobu ušao gospodin **Riedl** s riječima: „Dario, ideš kući.“ Kordić tada nije dobio nikakav papir ni rješenje o izlasku. Službeno rješenje stiglo mu je tek šest mjeseci kasnije. Taj trenutak uspoređuje s oslobađanjem **svetog Petra i svetog Pavla**, kada su se vrata, kako kaže, sama otvarala.

Vijest je saznao u utorak, dok su ga posjećivala trojica Hrvata, a let je bio predviđen za petak. Dušobrižnik ga je upozorio da će ga voziti „jednim jadnim autom“ kroz dvadesetak zatvora, od jutra do mraka, sve do **Beča**. Bio je to dan poplave u **Gunji**. Vladala je velika vrućina, a Kordić je sjedio stisnut uz jednog Mađara, bez vode. Ipak je zahvaljivao Bogu jer su ga sutradan čekali najbliži i već je bila dogovorena sveta misa u crkvi **svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci**.

### Noć s Afganistancem i Alžircem

Kordić se veselio što će posljednju noć provesti s Mađarom, no stražar ga je, nakon što su svjetla već bila ugašena, uveo u drugu sobu i najavio: „Ovaj će zatvorenik moliti se sad Bogu 15–20, pola sata i onda ćemo ugasiti svjetlo.“ Ispod deka dočekali su ga neprijateljski pogledi. Dobio je jedini krevet na kat u sobi.

Razgovor je počeo s mladim **Afganistancem**. Kordić mu je spomenuo da je u zatvoru imao dobrog prijatelja iz Afganistana, a pokazalo se da su njih dvojica prvi rođaci. Mladić mu je odmah ponudio pola svog kreveta i Bibliju da čita kod njega. U isto vrijeme cimer iz **Alžira**, očito u teškom stanju, tresao je krevet na kojem je Kordić trebao spavati i dozivao stražare tražeći ljude iz svoje zemlje. Stražari su ga smirili i tako je, kaže Kordić, „probio tu noć“.

### Križ kao „hladno oružje“

Sljedećeg jutra nije bilo konzula, nije bilo papira ni privremene putovnice. Ponovno je završio u **migracijskom zatvoru**, gdje su mu opet uzeli otiske prstiju i fotografirali ga. Već se pomirio s time da toga dana neće stići u Zagreb. Tada je zadihan stigao konzul, upalila su se rotirajuća svjetla i zrakoplov je zaustavljen. Na ulazu su mu križ oduzeli kao „**hladno oružje**“, a vratili su mu ga kasnije.

Za vrijeme leta pratio je zemljopis ispod sebe. Kad je ugledao **Dravu**, znao je da ulazi u Hrvatsku. „I to je sve ostalo onda povijest“, kaže.
sections.subtitle_en: The last night in prison, a stopped airplane, and the Drava beneath the wings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić recounts the last night in prison with an Afghan and an Algerian
sections.content_en:
Already the next day, Mr. **Riedl** entered his room with the words: "Dario, you are going home." At that time, Kordić did not receive any paper or decision regarding his release. The official decision arrived to him only six months later. He compares that moment to the liberation of **Saint Peter and Saint Paul**, when the doors, as he says, opened by themselves.

He learned the news on Tuesday, while three Croats were visiting him, and the flight was scheduled for Friday. The pastoral minister warned him that they would drive him in "a miserable car" through some twenty prisons, from morning to dark, all the way to **Beč**. It was the day of the flood in **Gunja**. Great heat prevailed, and Kordić sat squeezed next to a Hungarian, without water. Still, he thanked God because the next day his closest ones were waiting for him and Holy Mass had already been arranged in the church of **Saint Joseph on Trešnjevka**.

### A night with an Afghan and an Algerian

Kordić was looking forward to spending his last night with the Hungarian, but the guard, after the lights had already been turned off, brought him into another room and announced: "This prisoner will pray to God now for 15–20, half an hour, and then we will turn off the light." From under the blankets, hostile gazes met him. He received the only bunk bed in the room.

The conversation began with a young **Afghan**. Kordić mentioned to him that he had a good friend from Afghanistan in prison, and it turned out that the two of them were first cousins. The young man immediately offered him half of his bed and a Bible to read with him. At the same time, the roommate from **Algeria**, visibly in a difficult state, shook the bed on which Kordić was supposed to sleep and called out to the guards asking for people from his country. The guards calmed him down and thus, Kordić says, he "broke through that night."

### The cross as a "cold weapon"

The next morning there was no consul, there were no papers or temporary passport. He ended up in the **migration prison** again, where they took his fingerprints again and photographed him. He had already resigned himself to the fact that he would not arrive in Zagreb that day. Then the consul arrived out of breath, the rotating lights turned on, and the plane was stopped. At the entrance, they took away his cross as a "**cold weapon**", and returned it to him later.

During the flight, he observed the geography beneath him. When he caught sight of the **Drava**, he knew he was entering Croatia. "And all the rest of that then is history," he says.

sections.subtitle: Zavjet ispunjen u 60. godini: od „teologije na koljenima“ do diplome
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o zavjetu da upiše studij teologije ako izađe iz zatvora
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da je Kordić tih 17 godina zapravo „studirao teologiju na koljenima“, a ipak je iste godine kad je izašao upisao i formalni studij teologije. Pita je li to bio zavjet.

Kordić potvrđuje da jest. Kad je u zatvoru osjetio duhovni poziv, obećao je Gospodinu: ako bude imao priliku živjeti izvan zatvorskih zidina, upisat će taj studij. Kroz šalu dodaje da to nije učinio zato što nije imao što drugo raditi.

Bio je, kaže, **revan student**. U pet godina studija izostao je samo dva dana, zbog sprovoda. Nije tražio nikakve iznimke: pohađao je i tjelesni odgoj, i obilaske, i sve ostalo što su imali i drugi studenti. Uživao je u studiju i u njemu otkrio mnogo toga što prije nije znao.

Neki su ga ljudi zadirkivali da će „na studiju teologije izgubiti vjeru“. Kordić odgovara da ju je, Bogu hvala, ondje samo **produbio**. Diplomirao je u vrijeme korone, okružen mnogo mladih ljudi. Prvi fakultet završio je 1983. godine, u studentske klupe ponovno je sjeo nakon 31 godine, a drugi je fakultet završio **u 60. godini života**.
sections.subtitle_en: A vow fulfilled at age 60: from "theology on one's knees" to a diploma
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about the vow to enroll in theological studies if he got out of prison
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that during those 17 years Kordić was actually "studying theology on his knees," and yet in the very year he was released, he also enrolled in formal theological studies. He asks if that was a vow.

Kordić confirms that it was. When he felt a spiritual calling in prison, he promised the Lord: if he had the opportunity to live outside prison walls, he would enroll in those studies. He adds jokingly that he did not do it because he had nothing else to do.

He was, he says, a **zealous student**. In five years of study he missed only two days, due to a funeral. He did not ask for any exceptions: he attended physical education, and visits, and everything else that other students had too. He enjoyed his studies and discovered in them many things he had not known before.

Some people teased him that he would "lose his faith in theological studies." Kordić replies that, thank God, he only **deepened** it there. He graduated during the time of coronavirus, surrounded by many young people. He finished his first college in 1983, sat in student benches again after 31 years, and finished his second college **in the 60th year of his life**.

sections.subtitle: Javna molitva krunice i molitva za one s druge strane ograde
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o molitvi za prosvjednike tijekom javne muške molitve krunice
sections.content:
Nekoliko godina nakon povratka pokrenuta je **javna molitva krunice muškaraca**, a Kordić se među prvima pridružio. Krunoslav ga pita kako se kao javna osoba nosi s pozornošću medija, koji su ga, kaže voditelj, odmah „uočili i ulovili“.

Kordić kaže da je o tome često razgovarao sa suprugom i da su oboje bili istog mišljenja: on **ne bježi ni od koga**. Pojavit će se gdje treba, a nikome ne želi stvarati probleme. Molitvu je doživio kao „**Božji projekt**“ u kojem se muškarci, inače rijetko okupljeni u tolikom broju, okupljaju oko plemenite, duhovne misije.

Sjeća se prvih molitava, dok se još nije molilo na strani trga prema Franku, kad nije bilo ni banera ni toliko policije, a ni prosvjeda. Nije dolazio na svaku molitvu, ali bio je tri do četiri puta godišnje. Mediji su ga, kaže, primijetili jedno dvaput, a poslije im valjda više nije bilo zanimljivo pa su ga pustili na miru.

Isposlovaje da je, ponekad i predvodeći molitvu na mikrofonu, mnogo puta molio i **za prosvjednike**, da osjete Božju ljubav: „Evo, Gospodine, daj njih dotakni, pa da možda netko od njih dođe ovamo, pa da posvjedoči da je bio s one strane.“ Uvjeren je da bi takav čovjek bio prihvaćen s ljubavlju, jer „ima mjesta u Božjoj kući za svih“.

Krunoslav se nadovezuje pričom o jednom molitelju s trga koji kaže da je prosvjednika „premalo“. Volio bi da ih je što više, kako bi se što više njih obratilo od silnih molitava *Zdravo Marijo*. Kordić smatra da se obraćenja doista i događaju.
sections.subtitle_en: Public Rosary prayer and prayer for those on the other side of the fence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about praying for protesters during the public men's Rosary prayer
sections.content_en:
A few years after his return, the **public men's Rosary prayer** was launched, and Kordić was among the first to join. Krunoslav asks him how, as a public figure, he deals with the attention of the media, who, the host says, immediately "spotted and caught" him.

Kordić says that he often spoke about this with his wife and that they were both of the same opinion: he **does not run away from anyone**. He will show up where he needs to, and he does not want to cause problems for anyone. He experienced the prayer as "**God's project**" in which men, otherwise rarely gathered in such numbers, gather around a noble, spiritual mission.

He remembers the first prayers, while they were not yet praying on the side of the square toward Frank, when there were neither banners nor so much police, nor protests. He did not come to every prayer, but he attended three to four times a year. The media, he says, noticed him about twice, and later it was probably no longer interesting to them, so they left him alone.

He relates that, sometimes even leading the prayer on the microphone, he prayed many times **for the protesters** as well, that they may feel God's love: "Here, Lord, touch them, so that perhaps someone among them comes over here, to testify that he was on that other side." He is convinced that such a person would be received with love, because "there is room in God's house for all."

Krunoslav follows up with a story about a person praying from the square who says that there are "too few" protesters. He would like there to be as many of them as possible, so that as many of them as possible would convert from the countless *Hail Mary* prayers. Kordić believes that conversions indeed do happen.

sections.subtitle: Branitelji ispod mostova: pola tjedna za one koje je društvo zaboravilo
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić opisuje hrvatske branitelje koji spavaju na kolodvorima i ispod mostova
sections.content:
Kordić otkriva da se posljednjih četiri do pet godina ponajviše posvećuje **braniteljskoj populaciji**. Zajedno s bratom **Marinkom Šuškom**, u okviru **Mreže instituta** i s paterom **Mikom Mandurićem**, pokrenuo je inicijativu kojoj je cilj doći do hrvatskih branitelja **na rubu društva**. To su, kaže, ljudi koji „večeras spavaju na kolodvorima, na klupama, ispod mostova, u šupama“.

Razloga za takvu sudbinu ima, prema njegovim riječima, stotinu. Neki su nekad imali riješenu egzistenciju, drugi je nikad nisu imali. Zajedničko im je da trebaju **pruženu ruku** i nekoga tko će ih pokušati izvući uz Božju pomoć.

Aktivnosti uključuju:
- **duhovne obnove na Pašmanu**, u starom franjevačkom samostanu s paterom Mikom, koje traju već tri do četiri godine;
- obnove s **Kursiljom** i **Andrijom Vranom** na **Krapnju**, na koje dolaze i hrvatski branitelji;
- obilaske po cijeloj Hrvatskoj, od **Banovine i Slavonije** do **Dalmacije i Rijeke**, dok se mreža kontakata stalno širi.

Kordić procjenjuje da otprilike **pola svakog tjedna**, uz vrijeme za obitelj i unuke, posvećuje pomaganju braniteljima. Kaže da je u tome posebno sretan i da to ne doživljava samo kao ljubav, nego i kao svakodnevno suočavanje s konkretnim problemima za koje pokušava naći rješenja.

### Udruga Brat branitelj

Na Krunoslavovo pitanje Kordić potvrđuje da je riječ o **Udruzi Brat branitelj**, koja postoji otprilike godinu i pet mjeseci. Udruga surađuje s **Ministarstvom branitelja**, bez kojeg neke stvari nije moguće riješiti. Kordić priznaje da su u ministarstvu za svakoga za koga su došli pitati nastojali pomoći. „Istina što je istina, ja ću je reći“, kaže, dodajući da je nebitno što za vlastiti slučaj nekad nije naišao na razumijevanje, jer su važnija pitanja šire naravi.
sections.subtitle_en: Veterans under bridges: half a week for those whom society has forgotten
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić describes Croatian veterans who sleep at stations and under bridges
sections.content_en:
Kordić reveals that for the last four to five years he has been dedicating himself mostly to the **veteran population**. Together with brother **Marinko Šušak**, within the framework of **Mreža instituta** and with pater **Miko Mandurić**, he launched an initiative whose goal is to reach Croatian veterans **on the margins of society**. These are, he says, people who "tonight are sleeping at stations, on benches, under bridges, in sheds".

There are a hundred reasons for such a fate, according to his words. Some once had their livelihood resolved, others never did. What they have in common is that they need an **outstretched hand** and someone who will try to pull them out with God's help.

The activities include:
- **spiritual renewals on Pašman**, in an old Franciscan monastery with pater Miko, which have already been going on for three to four years;
- renewals with **Kursiljo** and **Andrija Vrana** on **Krapanj**, which are also attended by Croatian veterans;
- visits throughout Croatia, from **Banovina and Slavonija** to **Dalmacija and Rijeka**, while the network of contacts is constantly expanding.

Kordić estimates that roughly **half of each week**, alongside time for family and grandchildren, he devotes to helping veterans. He says he is particularly happy in this and that he does not experience it only as love, but also as a daily confrontation with concrete problems for which he tries to find solutions.

### Udruga Brat branitelj

To Krunoslav's question, Kordić confirms that this refers to **Udruga Brat branitelj**, which has existed for about a year and five months. The association cooperates with the **Ministarstvo branitelja**, without which some things cannot be resolved. Kordić admits that in the ministry, they strove to help everyone they came to ask about. "Truth is truth, I will say it," he says, adding that it is irrelevant that for his own case he did not once meet with understanding, because issues of a broader nature are more important.
keywords_en: veterans on the margins of society

sections.subtitle: „Ponovio bih“: što je Kordić zapravo rekao i zašto je i dalje na američkoj crnoj listi
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić objašnjava pravo značenje izjave „vrijedilo je, ponovio bih“
sections.content:
Krunoslav otvara osjetljivu temu. Prije nekoliko godina objavljen je novinski naslov prema kojem je Kordić navodno rekao da bi „sve ponovio“, a ta mu je rečenica „prišivena“ u kontekstu **Ahmića**. Voditelj ga moli da pojasni što je zapravo mislio.

Kordić najprije ironično primjećuje da mediji „bolje znaju što ja u srcu nosim nego ja“, dok srce svakoga čovjeka, kaže, zna samo Bog. Zatim objašnjava kontekst. Bio je upitan je li vrijedilo rata, zatvora i svih žrtava. Odgovorio je: „Vrijedilo je, **ponovio bih**, svaka je sekunda vrijedila.“ Smisao izjave, kaže, bio je osobni i duhovni: da nije prošao zatočeništvo, ne bi na takav način susreo Isusa Krista i bio bi „siromašan čovjek“.

### Na listi s Bin Ladenom

Istu je poruku, otkriva Kordić, uputio i jednoj **američkoj agenciji** koja prati rehabilitaciju bivših osuđenika. Ta ga agencija, kako navodi, i dalje drži na **crnoj listi**, zajedno s **Bin Ladenom** i sličnima. Godine **2017.** poslao im je dopis u kojem je naveo da studira teologiju i da nikome ne stvara probleme. Zamolio je da ga skinu s liste jer zbog nje, kaže, ne može normalno plaćati plin i struju, poslovati s bankom ni uopće funkcionirati.

Na odgovor je čekao **osam godina**. Stigao je prije otprilike pola godine do godine dana, a u njemu su ga pitali upravo kako može tvrditi da se rehabilitirao kad je izjavio da bi „ponovio“. Kordić im je odgovorio istim riječima kao i u podcastu: vrijedilo je sve što je prošao, jer bez toga ne bi susreo živoga Boga.
sections.subtitle_en: "I would do it again": what Kordić actually said and why he is still on the American blacklist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić explains the true meaning of the statement "it was worth it, I would do it again"
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav opens a sensitive topic. A few years ago, a newspaper headline was published according to which Kordić allegedly said that he would "do it all again," and that sentence was "pinned" on him in the context of **Ahmići**. The host asks him to clarify what he actually meant.

Kordić first ironically remarks that the media "know better what I carry in my heart than I do," while every person's heart, he says, is known only to God. Then he explains the context. He was asked whether the war, prison, and all the sacrifices were worth it. He replied: "It was worth it, **I would do it again**, every second was worth it." The meaning of the statement, he says, was personal and spiritual: if he had not gone through imprisonment, he would not have encountered Jesus Christ in such a way and would be a "poor man."

### On the list with Bin Laden

The same message, Kordić reveals, was also sent to an **American agency** that monitors the rehabilitation of former convicts. That agency, as he states, still keeps him on a **blacklist**, together with **Bin Laden** and the like. In **2017**, he sent them a letter stating that he was studying theology and causing problems for no one. He asked to be removed from the list because, due to it, he says, he cannot normally pay for gas and electricity, do business with a bank, or function at all.

He waited **eight years** for an answer. It arrived about half a year to a year ago, and in it they asked him precisely how he could claim that he was rehabilitated when he stated that he would "do it again." Kordić answered them with the same words as in the podcast: everything he went through was worth it, because without it he would not have encountered the living God.

sections.subtitle: Tri medijska nastupa u dvanaest godina i isprika nakon Pompejske pobožnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić govori o suprugi koja je molila za klevetnike i o primljenoj isprici
sections.content:
Kordić naglašava da do ovog podcasta nikada nije javno demantirao napise o sebi. Ovo mu je tek **treći medijski nastup u dvanaest godina** na slobodi:
- prvi je bio na jednoj svjetovnoj televiziji kod urednice **Ozane**, gdje se razgovaralo o općim temama, a on je u studio donio križ i krunicu pa je emisija, kako kaže, ispala duhovna;
- drugi je bio prije otprilike godinu i pol kod patera **Ike** u **Magis institutu**;
- treći je ovaj podcast.

Obitelj Kordić, ističe, u **33 godine** nije odgovorila ni na jednu objedu ni laž. Sve nose strpljivo. Ako ne dobiju barem četiri do pet napada godišnje, on se, kaže, zabrine.

### „Molim se za ljude koji ovo pljuju“

U vrijeme najžešćih napada pater Ike pozvao je supružnike na razgovor i molitvu. Kordić napominje da tada još nije redovito molio s njim, a sada ondje ima termin četvrtkom u molitvi „**Krunica Hrvata svega svijeta**“. Venera je tom prilikom rekla: „Pater Ike, ja se molim za ljude koji ovo pljuju, da im Gospodin dotakne njihovo srce.“

Kordić priznaje da se za neke ljude čini kako ne vrijedi ni moliti, no pokazalo se drukčije. Supruga je molila **Pompejsku pobožnost**: 27 dana krunice na nakanu i 27 dana zahvale. Predzadnjeg dana Kordiću je stigla poruka preko prijatelja koji je nekoć bio visoko pozicioniran, „najviše u Bosni i Hercegovini u svoja vremena“. Poruku je slao čovjek koji ga je na jednom portalu godinama ponajviše napadao. Pitao je može li mu Kordić oprostiti što ga je dvanaest godina tako blatio, jer je u međuvremenu proučio neke stvari i postalo ga je sram.

Kordić mu je poslao oprost i zaključuje: „Supruga je to izmolila. Znači, **nema izgubljenih slučajeva**.“
sections.subtitle_en: Three media appearances in twelve years and an apology after the Pompeian devotion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić speaks about his wife who prayed for slanderers and about the apology received
sections.content_en:
Kordić emphasizes that until this podcast he had never publicly denied articles about himself. This is only his **third media appearance in twelve years** of freedom:
- the first was on a secular television station with editor **Ozana**, where general topics were discussed, and he brought a cross and a Rosary into the studio so the show, as he says, turned out to be spiritual;
- the second was about a year and a half ago with pater **Ike** at the **Magis institut**;
- the third is this podcast.

The Kordić family, he points out, has not responded to a single slander or lie in **33 years**. They bear everything patiently. If they do not receive at least four to five attacks a year, he says, he gets worried.

### "I pray for the people who spit on this"

At the time of the fiercest attacks, pater Ike invited the spouses for a conversation and prayer. Kordić notes that back then he did not yet pray regularly with him, and now he has a slot there on Thursdays in the prayer "**Krunica Hrvata svega svijeta**". On that occasion, Venera said: "Pater Ike, I pray for the people who spit on this, that the Lord would touch their heart."

Kordić admits that for some people it seems not even worth praying, but it turned out differently. His wife prayed the **Pompeian devotion**: 27 days of the Rosary for an intention and 27 days of thanksgiving. On the penultimate day, a message reached Kordić via a friend who was once highly positioned, "the highest in Bosna i Hercegovina in his time". The message was sent by a man who had attacked him the most on a portal for years. He asked if Kordić could forgive him for smearing him like that for twelve years, because in the meantime he had studied some things and became ashamed.

Kordić sent him forgiveness and concludes: "My wife obtained that through prayer. That means, **there are no lost causes**."

sections.subtitle: „Hrvatska s Kristom“ i blic pitanja: križ, zavičaj, sveci i Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description: Dario Kordić odgovara na blic pitanja voditelja Krunoslava
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora Krunoslav traži od gosta poruku. Kordić se obraća Hrvatima koji gledaju podcast:

> „Ukoliko smo s Kristom kao Hrvatska, ne trebamo ništa dvojiti, bojati se, samo budimo s Kristom, sve će onda biti i Hrvatska će biti na mjestu. Ukoliko mi nismo s Kristom, onda bilo što oko nas može biti najljepše, to nema vrijednosti.“

Uslijedila su **blic pitanja** s dvije ponuđene opcije, za koja voditelj unaprijed napominje da su „malo provokativna, malo zeznuta“.

**Krunica u ruci ili križ oko vrata?** Kordić bira **križ**. Ljubi ga jer mu je Gospodin pokazao da bez križa nema vječnoga života, a zahvaljivao je, kaže, na svim križevima.

**Busovača ili Zagreb?** Odgovara „**i jedno i drugo**“. Zavičaj, Žepče i Busovača, uvijek je u srcu, ali svaki dio Hrvatske doživljava kao svoj i nema sela u kojem ne osjeti radost. Posebno spominje **svetog Antu Padovanskog**, zaštitnika Busovače, i kip **Kuzme Kovačića** koji je četiri godine nakon rata imao priliku vidjeti.

**Sveti Ante ili Gospa?** Kordić izabire **Gospu**, ali dodaje da je na prvom mjestu **Krist**, a tek kroz Krista sveti Ante i Gospa. Prije je bio posebno vezan uz svetog Antu, no otkad je s obitelji u župi **svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci**, upoznao je, kaže, milosti koje se mogu izmoliti po svetom Josipu, „toliko moćnom svecu koji je Krista odgajao“. Krunoslav dodaje da se u to svatko mora sam uvjeriti.

**Mariazell ili Međugorje?** Kordić bira **Međugorje**. Ističe da nismo svjesni kolika je milost kroz Međugorje došla cijelom svijetu i da je **Međugorska Majka** njega osobno snažno pratila. Kad Krunoslav primijeti da se Gospa „ukazala kao Hercegovka“, Kordić to potvrđuje, ali upozorava da Hrvati zbog toga ne smiju biti „bahati“, jer je riječ o milosti koja se „ne može riječima opisati“.
sections.subtitle_en: “Croatia with Christ” and blitz questions: the cross, native region, saints, and Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: Dario Kordić answers blitz questions from host Krunoslav
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, Krunoslav asks the guest for a message. Kordić addresses the Croats watching the podcast:

> “If we are with Christ as Croatia, we do not need to doubt anything, to fear, let us just be with Christ, then everything will be and Croatia will be in its place. If we are not with Christ, then anything around us can be the most beautiful, it has no value.”

There followed **blitz questions** with two offered options, which the host notes in advance are “a little provocative, a little tricky”.

**Rosary in hand or cross around the neck?** Kordić chooses the **cross**. He loves it because the Lord showed him that without the cross there is no eternal life, and he gave thanks, he says, for all crosses.

**Busovača or Zagreb?** He answers “**both**”. His native region, Žepče and Busovača, is always in his heart, but he experiences every part of Croatia as his own and there is no village in which he does not feel joy. He especially mentions **Saint Anthony of Padua**, the patron saint of Busovača, and the statue by **Kuzma Kovačić** which he had the opportunity to see four years after the war.

**Saint Anthony or Our Lady?** Kordić chooses **Our Lady**, but adds that **Christ** is in the first place, and only through Christ Saint Anthony and Our Lady. Previously he was particularly attached to Saint Anthony, but since he has been with his family in the parish of **Saint Joseph in Trešnjevka**, he has come to know, he says, the graces that can be obtained through prayer through Saint Joseph, “such a powerful saint who raised Christ”. Krunoslav adds that everyone must see this for themselves.

**Mariazell or Međugorje?** Kordić chooses **Međugorje**. He points out that we are not aware of how much grace has come to the entire world through Međugorje and that the **Mother of Međugorje** has strongly accompanied him personally. When Krunoslav remarks that Our Lady “appeared as a Herzegovinian woman”, Kordić confirms it, but warns that Croats must not be “arrogant” because of that, because it is a grace that “cannot be described in words”.

sections.subtitle: Zahvale na kraju i najava: molitva umjesto osvete
sections.screenshot_description: Gost sljedeće epizode u najavi govori o napadu i molitvi za napadača
sections.content:
Krunoslav zahvaljuje „dragom bratu“ na gostovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je Kordićevo svjedočanstvo mnogima progovorilo, potaknulo ih na razmišljanje i možda promijenilo sliku koju su o njemu imali. Kordić uzvraća zahvalom Gospodinu na tom danu i emisiji, uz želju da „dotakne mnoga srca“, te zahvaljuje voditelju što je razgovor vodio „u Duhu Svetom“.

Voditelj zatim poziva gledatelje da podrže podcast **Redefinicija** lajkanjem, dijeljenjem, pretplatom na YouTube kanal te novčano i molitveno. Napominje da se sljedeća epizoda može pogledati odmah putem profila na **Patreonu**, bez čekanja mjesec dana.

### Najava sljedeće epizode

U kratkom isječku **gost sljedeće epizode** prepričava kako je napadnut na javnom mjestu, nakon čega je policija obavila očevid. Umjesto uzvraćanja on i njegovi bližnji odlučili su **moliti za napadača**. To naziva „poantom Božje pedagogije“: nisu išli „na mišiće“, nego „na Božji način“. Nakon nekog vremena napadač je uplatio prilog župniku za crkvu, nazvao ga telefonom i zamolio za oprost. Najava se tako tematski nadovezuje na poruku kojom je Kordić zaključio svoje svjedočanstvo: da nema izgubljenih slučajeva.
sections.subtitle_en: Thanks at the end and announcement: prayer instead of revenge
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest of the next episode in the preview talks about an attack and prayer for the attacker
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav thanks his "dear brother" for the guest appearance and expresses conviction that Kordić's testimony spoke to many, prompted them to reflect, and perhaps changed the image they had of him. Kordić responds with thanks to the Lord for that day and the show, with the desire that it "touches many hearts", and thanks the host for leading the conversation "in the Holy Spirit".

The host then invites viewers to support the **Redefinicija** podcast by liking, sharing, subscribing to the YouTube channel, and financially and prayerfully. He notes that the next episode can be watched immediately via the **Patreon** profile, without waiting a month.

### Announcement of the next episode

In a short clip, **the guest of the next episode** recounts how he was attacked in a public place, after which the police conducted an investigation. Instead of retaliating, he and those close to him decided to **pray for the attacker**. He calls this the "point of God's pedagogy": they did not go "by muscle", but "in God's way". After some time, the attacker made a donation to the parish priest for the church, called him by phone, and asked for forgiveness. The preview thus thematically builds upon the message with which Kordić concluded his testimony: that there are no lost cases.
